items.article_title: Nodal signaling establishes a competency window for stochastic cell fate switching
items.note: The quote (the 2022 article's own abstract conclusion; its title states the same finding) describes a stochastic fate switch inside a competence window, which speaks to the question's 'only some cells become endoderm'. One study's conclusion is labelled settled; whether the field treats it so is not in the quote, and the question as a whole (how the pattern becomes fates) is wider.

items.article_title: Knockout of thyroid hormone receptor alpha a (thraa) enhances cardiac regeneration in zebrafish through metabolic and hypoxic regulation
items.note: The quote asserts that elevated thyroid hormone and metabolism promote cardiomyocyte cycle exit and polyploidization, limiting regeneration. The cited 2025 article is a single zebrafish knockout study (title); the quote does not show that it settles the mammal-versus-zebrafish difference the question asks about.

items.article_title: Impaired fin regeneration and angiogenesis in aged zebrafish and turquoise killifish
items.note: The quote supports reduced regeneration with age, in 'both species'; the article title shows these are zebrafish and turquoise killifish, so the zebrafish age facet is supported by one 2023 study. The repeated-amputation part and 'under what conditions' of the question are not addressed by the quote.

items.locator: Announcing the Rule 30 Prizes > The Rule 30 Prize Problems > Problem 1: Does the center column always remain non-periodic?
items.note: The quote states that periodicity is unproven beyond the first billion steps and that a proof is needed. It matches the question. This is a mathematics prize problem on a blog announcement, sitting in a biology register; its attestation is not biology literature.

items.article_title: Zebrafish Vascular Mural Cell Biology: Recent Advances, Development, and Functions
items.locator: 3. Mural Cell Development in Zebrafish > 3.1. Overview of Mural Cell Development during the Early Developmental Stages in Zebrafish
items.note: The quote supports the second half of the question (how and when veins acquire mural coverage is little known, in a 2021 review). The first half, what restricts recruitment to arteries, is not in the quote.

items.article_title: Control of organ size: development, regeneration, and the role of theory in biology
items.note: A 2015 commentary says how organ sizes stay proportionate 'remains mysterious'. It matches the question; it is an opinion in a perspective piece, as of 2015.

items.article_title: Spatiotemporal control of pattern formation during somitogenesis
items.locator: INTRODUCTION > FUTURE DIRECTIONS > The decoding and execution of spatiotemporal information
items.note: The quote says reconstruction of the gene regulatory network executing somite segmentation in the anterior presomitic mesoderm is 'not completely resolved' (2024 review). The named Tbx6, Mesp and Ripply network and the clock-to-boundary step are not in the quote, so it supports a nearby open area more than this specific question.

items.article_title: From Stripes to a Beating Heart: Early Cardiac Development in Zebrafish
items.note: The quote states that it is unclear to what extent arterial and venous pole derivatives share a common progenitor pool in the early lateral plate mesoderm (2021 review). This closely matches the question.

items.article_title: The Physical Basis of Coordinated Tissue Spreading in Zebrafish Gastrulation
items.note: The quote says the mechanisms of radial intercalation are 'not yet fully understood' and itself cites a 2010 review, inside a 2017 article, so the openness statement is dated to the 2010 literature. The question's second part (how much is a response to enveloping-layer expansion) is not in the quote.

items.article_title: Molecular Dating of the Teleost Whole Genome Duplication (3R) Is Compatible With the Expectations of Delayed Rediploidization
items.note: The quote says the dating results remain compatible with a prolonged rediploidization process, which 'remains a viable mechanism' for teleost novelties (the 2024 article's title also says its dating is 'compatible with' delayed rediploidization). That is a statement of compatibility, not a statement that the causal question is unresolved, so a stance of 'open' is not supported by this quote.

items.article_title: Mechanical Stretch and PI3K Signaling Link Cell Migration and Proliferation to Coordinate Epithelial Tubule Morphogenesis in the Zebrafish Pronephros
items.note: The quote says the precise mechanism linking cell stretch to proliferation 'is not known' (2012 article). It matches the question; the openness is as of 2012 and later work was not checked.

items.article_title: Combined mutations of hoxa13a, hoxa13b, and hoxd13a lead to structural shifts in zebrafish soft fin rays providing insight into spiny ray evolution
items.note: The quote says how spines arose, and why fin ray structure differs in some species, 'remains to be fully understood' (2026 article). It matches the question.

items.article_title: Caudal fin shape imprinted during late zebrafish embryogenesis is re-patterned by the Sonic hedgehog pathway

epithelial-repair.title: Epithelial repair patch
epithelial-repair.mission: Ask one question about a cultured epithelial sheet: how do cell-level motility and mechanics set the closure of a gap, and what barrier geometry results? A bounded proposal. Two published mechanics models define what is known. The Morpheus engine run here is named as a possible instrument. No wound simulation exists in this node yet.
limitations: Every member ref is a snapshot-catalog ref (namespace 'snapshot'), not a live-store version: re-pin before submitting.
The cited papers have no record in the catalog, so they are not members. They appear as sources on the page, read at abstract level only.
No calibration bridges any pair of scales; every coupling is absent or scenario-level.
No runner exists for this project; every instrument is proposed. Nothing here is a simulation or an observation.

scale_coverage.note: Protrusion and contractility are inputs of the published models; none is modelled here.
Two abstracts describe cell mechanics and adhesion; no parameter is sourced here.
Two published models of closure are known at abstract level; none has been run here.

requirements.text: In a declared stress-free, force-balanced model with no other active drive, setting protrusion intensity to zero leaves closed area constant to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: Closure anyway triggers diagnosis, not a presumed defect: passive relaxation, initial stress, cell-cell or cell-substrate forces or another active mechanism can legitimately close a gap. No mechanism is read from the run until the cause is found.

Closure efficiency changes with initial gap size and with protrusion intensity, as Bai and Zeng report. The abstract gives no direction, so none is assumed. Falsified if: A run that shows no dependence on either does not reproduce the reported dependence.

Paired runs from the same initial state give closed area within tolerance when dt (and grid, where there is one) is refined. Cell count is also preserved only under a declared no-birth, no-death assumption. Seed-to-seed variability is reported as an ensemble spread, not tested for equality. Falsified if: A paired change larger than the tolerance voids the comparison for that setup. Variation across independent seeds is not by itself a defect.
This project is not a clinical treatment or wound-care claim; not a viable engineered organism; not observed wound healing in any fish tissue; not evidence for fin regeneration.

open_questions.text: What evidence would connect a lower-scale prediction to tissue-scale closure in one named cell line? (The same shape of gap as the registered question F002.)
Is closure efficiency against gap size comparable between a Cellular Potts and a continuum model once both are calibrated to one measurement?
What barrier-geometry readout (remaining gap shape) is worth measuring beyond closed area?

flying-fish.title: Engineer toward a flying fish
flying-fish.mission: Engineer toward a flying fish: explore, with typed models and refusals, what a flying-fish-like glider would require. This is a design-studio project on a generic schema; it does not assert that any design is feasible.
limitations: Every member ref is a snapshot-catalog ref (namespace 'snapshot'), not a live-store version: re-pin before submitting.
Membership is a declared pin and states where a record applies; it infers no causal link between members.
No calibration bridges any pair of scales; every coupling above the organ scale is refused or assumption-level.
The numeric requirements are Fish 1990 observed ranges proposed as a design envelope, not a feasibility certificate.

scale_coverage.note: One molecule-to-fin source (Daane 2021, association in zebrafish); no executable model, no parameter link to wing area.
No structure or affinity input for a fin-patterning protein; the one binding test was stopped at its coverage floor.
A two-cell Delta-Notch model is replayed in this project but it is non-dimensional and not tied to a fish; no cell-to-fin coupling exists.

Darwin 1859, a phylogeny and a fossil source as context; no ecological model.

What is the effective flexural rigidity of an excised fin ray under the clamping that matches its in-fin boundary condition? The beam model sweeps an assumed range.
Is there a sourced upper size limit for a gliding fish? Davenport 2003, the paper that argues one, is unread.

tissue-microcarrier.title: Contractile tissue microcarrier
tissue-microcarrier.mission: Ask one question about a Xenopus-inspired contractile tissue construct: how does a chosen actuation pattern turn into deformation, and how much of that deformation becomes net motion? A bounded proposal. A generic soft-body mechanics runner and existing cell-scale tools are named as instruments. No simulation of this construct exists in this node yet, and no frog or fish parameter is used.

requirements.text: With actuation off, from zero initial velocity and a settled force-balanced shape, with no external flow or forcing, a defined reference frame and after a stated transient window, net displacement is zero to numerical tolerance. Falsified if: A nonzero passive displacement under those stated conditions triggers diagnosis of the setup or the runner. If a condition was not met, the control is restated, not read as a defect. No other endpoint is read until it is resolved.

Two predeclared patterns with equal total actuation give net displacements that differ by more than a dt or mesh refinement changes either one. Falsified if: If the difference is smaller than the refinement change, no pattern-to-motion statement is made.
A mirrored pattern on a symmetric body gives the mirrored displacement. Falsified if: A failure marks an anisotropy artifact in the body or the solver.
This project is not a designed living organism or a release claim; not a clinical or medical claim; not a fish tissue, or part of the flying-fish design; not frog-validated mechanics.

why_this_one: It is the only item that both removes an explicit essential blocker (tissue-to-EI) and has a stated measurement in the owning handoff.

design_review.note: Source-only review prompts written from this repository's own project projection and model-coupling report. They are not challenges by reviewers, not new findings and not biological observations. Replace them with Project records and real annotations when the node serves them.
design_review.meaning: A design review is an authored, falsifiable challenge attached to one exact Project version. It is not a vote, consensus score, answer, scientific adjudication or project resolution. A reply does not change the challenged Project.

source_prompts.title: Fin-beam load bridge is scenario-level
source_prompts.observation: The organ panel calls the fin-beam model a scoped elastic surrogate. docs/model-coupling.md marks the load-to-beam bridge scenario-level: mean lift-pressure proxy times a declared tributary width, a declared ray-length fraction and an assumed EI. There is no calibrated fin stiffness or measured ray pressure.
source_prompts.ask: Which loading regime and measured stiffness would falsify this bridge?

source_prompts.title: Notch/Delta to fin stiffness is refused
source_prompts.observation: The coupling report refuses the Collier Notch/Delta to fin-stiffness bridge: there is no mapping, and the transfer spans cell-to-organ and taxon contexts.
source_prompts.ask: What exact, context-matched developmental or tissue measurement would be required before this counts as a biological bridge?

source_prompts.title: Zebrafish interaction phenocopies fin proportion; transfer to halfbeaks unestablished
source_prompts.observation: The Daane 2021 zebrafish interaction phenocopies flying-fish fin proportion, but transfer to halfbeaks is unestablished and no developmental model connects adult proportions to a program.
source_prompts.ask: Which test separates correlation from the asserted genotype-to-fin pathway, with exact source and model pins?

source_prompts.title: Glide release convention drives much of the range
source_prompts.observation: The glide report uses a release at 1.5 times stall speed from 1 m, equivalent to release heights from about 1.8 m to 32.6 m. It says this convention drives much of the range and is a model artifact.
source_prompts.ask: Compare a sourced fixed-speed or fixed-height release; what observable would reject either?

general_prompts.text: Identify which measured animal, life stage and loading regime justify the modeled fin stiffness; if none is pinned, say unknown and propose a test.
Challenge a ray-to-fin mapping at a specific Project member and cite an exact mesh or source record; say whether the geometry is measured, reconstructed or illustrative.
Separate a level-flight lift constraint from glide and sink predictions; name the regime and the evidence that would falsify the proxy.
Require an exact developmental or genetic Evidence pin before treating a morphology correlation as a causal genotype-to-fin link.
State print material, orientation, minimum feature size and a physical test that could reject the design claim.

examples.passage:
[Wikipedia, Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, wikitext]
Euler–Bernoulli beam theory is limited to small deflections of a [[beam (structure)|beam]] that is subjected to lateral loads only, causing [[Elasticity (physics)|elastic]] bending.
| colspan="2" | '''Cantilever beam with end load'''
| rowspan="4" |[[File:CantBeamPointLoad.svg|350px]]
|-
| <math>M(x) = P(L-x)</math>
| <math>M_A = PL</math>
|-
| <math>Q(x) = P </math>
| <math>Q_{\mathrm{max}} = P</math>
|-
| <math>w(x) = \tfrac{Px^2(3L-x)}{6EI} </math>
| <math>w_C = \tfrac{PL^3}{3EI}</math>

[Alben, Madden & Lauder 2007, PMC2359861, Section 3 text]
In our experiment, we have found using three-point bending tests that the ‘composite’ Young's modulus corresponding to the whole structure is E ≈10 8 –10 9 N m −2 , with the average area moment of inertia I ≈10 −6 cm 4 . Hence, the measured B = EI ≈10 −6 –10 −5 J m.
examples.note: The expected result is a checked proposal with a witness; translation fidelity is still unresolved.

claim.text: Tip deflection of a clamped-free beam under a point load P at the free end is w_C = P L^3 / (3 E I); the fin-ray uses E ~ 1e8-1e9 N m^-2 and I ~ 1e-6 cm^4 (Alben et al. 2007).

assumptions.text: The passage equates B to EI. The unit J m is equivalent to N m^2.
Rewrote w_C = PL^3 / (3EI) as 3 * E * I * w_C = P * L^3 to comply with grammar rules regarding division.

unresolved.question: The passage provides a range for B (10^-6 to 10^-5 J m) and E (10^8 to 10^9 N m^-2) but a single value for I (10^-6 cm^4). The product of the lower bounds of E and I (10^8 * 10^-14 = 10^-6) matches the lower bound of B, but the upper bound of B (10^-5) is not reached unless I or E varies further.

examples.passage:
[Wikipedia, Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, wikitext]
Euler–Bernoulli beam theory is limited to small deflections of a [[beam (structure)|beam]] that is subjected to lateral loads only, causing [[Elasticity (physics)|elastic]] bending.
| colspan="2" | '''Cantilever beam with end load'''
| rowspan="4" |[[File:CantBeamPointLoad.svg|350px]]
|-
| <math>M(x) = P(L-x)</math>
| <math>M_A = PL</math>
|-
| <math>Q(x) = P </math>
| <math>Q_{\mathrm{max}} = P</math>
|-
| <math>w(x) = \tfrac{Px^2(3L-x)}{6EI} </math>
| <math>w_C = \tfrac{PL^3}{3EI}</math>

[Alben, Madden & Lauder 2007, PMC2359861, Section 3 text]
In our experiment, we have found using three-point bending tests that the ‘composite’ Young's modulus corresponding to the whole structure is E ≈10 8 –10 9 N m −2 , with the average area moment of inertia I ≈10 −6 cm 4 . Hence, the measured B = EI ≈10 −6 –10 −5 J m.

examples.title: Recorded Gemini proposal oca2-gemini-1

claim.text: Loss of oca2 exon 21 in Molino cavefish explains their albinism.

source.ref: Warren et al. 2021 Nat Commun, PMC7933363 (Europe PMC full text)

assumptions.text: The percentage 46.5% is the empirical ratio of albino offspring observed in the cross.

constraints.source_ref: 46.5% of the offspring completely lacked pigment ( n = 40/86 )

source_mapping.quote: 46.5% of the offspring completely lacked pigment ( n = 40/86, Supplementary Fig. 5j )

unresolved.question: The passage claims a change in the oca2 locus is responsible for albinism, but no mathematical mechanism for the genetic inheritance or the biochemical pathway is provided.
The value 46.5% (40/86) is approximately 0.4651; the passage rounds this to one decimal place.

examples.passage:
[Warren et al. 2021, Nat Commun, PMC7933363, Results (Europe PMC full-text XML, tags stripped)]
Consistent with the laboratory strains, exon 21 of oca2 is absent in all Molino cavefish samples ( n = 9, Supplementary Fig. 8 ).
We further functionally verified that a change in the oca2 locus is responsible for albinism in the F 2 hybrids, by crossing an albino surface/Pachón F 2 hybrid with a genetically engineered surface fish heterozygous for a deletion in oca2 exon 21 27 . We found that 46.5% of the offspring completely lacked pigment ( n = 40/86, Supplementary Fig. 5j ). This confirms that a change in the oca2 locus is responsible for loss of pigment in the mapping population.

forms.title: Reinforced display prop of fish3d-v3c-daane-length
forms.why: stronger handling prop: 1.5 mm wall rule (membranes 1.8 mm, rays 3.3 to 2.4 mm) and every fin 1.5 x as thick at its root, tapering to the plain fin 8 mm out, where a cantilevered fin's bending moment is largest

limitations: Print preparation is unvalidated: printer and resin are unknown; nothing has been sliced, loaded into PreForm or printed.

Wall rules are provisional, configurable prop choices (1.0 mm; 1.5 mm for the reinforced prop), checked on sampled faces only (3,000 plus 12,000 samples, or every face of a mesh with fewer faces); a thinner region between samples can be missed.
Membranes and rays are thickened for printing; they are not biological thickness. Flow and fin-ray work use the 1:1 candidate files, not these props.

The -scales file adds 0.2-0.4 mm scale and gill-cover relief: texture below the wall rule by design, not gated by it; whether it resolves depends on the unknown printer. The smooth file is the gated one.
Closed, oriented, single-piece manifold, positive volume and box fit are checked on every file; global self-intersection is not checked.
Engineered illustrative forms: not organisms and not a living or bio-printed construct.
Masses are calculated from mesh volume at the Alpha Grey V1 card density (1220 kg/m3, cured); the prop resin is not chosen and nothing was weighed.
Minimum wall 1.0 mm is a provisional, configurable prop choice, checked on sampled faces only; a thinner region between samples can be missed.

data.grounding_note: A law listed for a file says how the file relates to it (governing, checked, inspired_only, not_applicable); it is not evidence that the printed shape satisfies the law. Masses are calculated from mesh volume times a card density and were not weighed. No part has been printed, weighed, glided or thrown; no launch is cleared; the lift, drag, stability, beam and catch numbers are hand models or simulated scenarios with assumed coefficients (C_L in particular depends on geometry and flow and generally comes from experiment). Failed thresholds are reported as failed. Frozen revisions are read, never edited; inconsistencies in their prose are listed under findings, not corrected.

relation.governing: the law computed a number reported for these bytes (the computation is in the evidence)
relation.checked: a stated check against this law or rule was executed on these bytes; its outcome is in checks[]
relation.inspired_only: the law or source shaped the design; nothing here checks these bytes against it
relation.not_applicable: the law does not apply to this file; the detail says why

check_status.pass: executed on these bytes and met its stated threshold
check_status.fail: executed and did not meet its threshold (never relaxed)
check_status.unresolved: executed, with a reading or reviewer finding that the threshold does not settle
check_status.unknown: not determinable from these bytes (for example the resin is not chosen)
check_status.not_applicable: does not apply; the detail says why
check_status.withdrawn: the file is not to be printed; the detail says why

laws.scope: Axis-aligned permutations only. Glider: 200 x 125 x 235 mm less 5 mm a side (root-confirmed envelope, assumed margin). Props: 120 mm box. Printer compatibility is not claimed.

laws.title: A right part is the mirror image of its left part
laws.scope: Glider paired fins: a print cannot be reflected, so a right file holding the left part prints a second left fin. print-v4 props (one solid each): the solid equals its own y-mirror, vol(M \ mirror_y M) / vol(M) <= 1e-3, so the right fins are the left fins mirrored.

evidence.what: vertex-set comparison of every _L/_R print pair
y-mirror symmetric difference of every print-v4 STL

laws.title: No extremity thinner than the wall rod (no needle tips)
laws.scope: A design rule (not a printer limit): at every convex-hull vertex cluster (2 mm), the material within 3 mm is at least a rod of wall-rule diameter and 3 mm length. Extremities inside the hull, such as the caudal fork's inner corner, are not tested. Run on print-v4 only.

findings.detail: Every _R print STL of r1-r3 holds the left part (det -1 export pose). Kept byte for byte; fixed in r4-daane-printfix. Fish-frame mass properties, GLBs and flight models were not affected.

Reviewer claude-13: readings down to 0.097 mm (0.115 mm twice on r3) at the x 20 slot's lateral openings, judged feather edges rather than a thin wall; they can print rough, chip, or cut the band. The builder's sampler classed its own 0.31 mm reading there as edge-limited and did not gate it. r1's body has a reviewer reading of 0.317 mm aft of its catch slot, also edge-limited.

biological_constraints.kept reads 'v3a outline, ray count, ray roots, angles and lengths, fin positions and dihedral', but source_candidate is fish3d-v3c-daane-length. claim_reuse.readme:
# Actual Claim reuse through two leased computations

One existing exact public Claim was consumed before two distinct bounded
computations, with actual MCP proposals, coordinator readiness, leases, running
states, proposed Evidence and submitted Actions. Independent review is pending;
the producer has not accepted any record. This demonstrates scoped input reuse
and a contribution workflow, not collective benefit or calibrated fish biology.

The shared [Claim read](claim-read.json) pins
`node-a/Claim/eng-finmech-claim-ei-crit@4998ef85bd98ec64c0f4bc86e77337ea25df7ff5683ac6b62dc9095cf5f62f57`.
Its exact rational stiffness threshold is parsed at runtime and multiplied by the
predeclared margin to construct the solver's actual EI input. There is no fallback
hardcoded candidate stiffness. [Protocol](protocol.json) was committed in
`be4dfc6` before candidate solver runs. The current producer result file differs
from the Claim's named source: the [historical result](source-result.json) was
retrieved from the exact source commit and matches its digest; the
[request](source-request.json) matches the original canonical input hash.

| Distinct candidate | Consumed EI (N m²) | Computed tip/span | Maximum slope (rad) | Declared linear-model domain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Below threshold, 9/10 × Claim threshold | 11907/20480000 | 0.111111111158 | 0.148148148207 | Invalid; retained counterexample |
| Above threshold, 11/10 × Claim threshold | 14553/20480000 | 0.090909090883 | 0.121212121180 | Inside declared limits |

The declared limits are tip/span≤0.1 and slope≤0.2 rad. Both runs passed the frozen
quadrature, zero-load, wrong-law mutation, FEM/analytic and grid/profile checks.
Maximum FEM tip relative errors were 4.22e-10 and 2.88e-10 against the fixed 1e-6
limit. Static FEM used 16, 32 and 64 elements; there is no time step. Actual
compute/control wall times were approximately 0.486 and 0.459 seconds, excluding
MCP transport and preparation. No cloud or GPU job was used.

![Actual saved profiles](candidate-profiles.png)

The existing load bridge and beam solver were reused. All pressure, geometry,
material and validity inputs remain declared illustration assumptions. The
invalid lower candidate is not a biological deformation prediction. Empirical
validation and biological success remain unknown; no success probability,
time/cost saving or agency advantage is assigned.

## Inspectable evidence

- [Audit](audit.json) verifies exact Record digests, producer links, artifact
  bytes, code/protocol pins and chronological Claim-read→input-binding→solver→
  Evidence ordering. It counts two distinct current Action **ids**, not merely
  repeated versions. Its chronology uses producer-witnessed UTC, not an external
  time anchor.
- [Typed uses edges](reuse-verification.json) were read back from the live MCP
  neighborhood; the graph was not truncated. [Public catalog readback](public-catalog-readback.json)
  independently returns both current Action heads as submitted.
- Per-case [lower result](below-threshold/result.json) and
  [higher result](above-threshold/result.json), effective inputs, actual profile
  CSVs, exact pre-run Claim reads, proposed Evidence receipts and submitted Action
  readbacks retain the numerical and workflow details.
- [Execution plan](execution-plan.json), [code pins](code-pin.json),
  [environment](environment.json) and safe MCP transcripts preserve provenance.
  Credentials and lease capabilities are excluded/redacted.
- [Superseded proposals](superseded-proposals.json) preserve one correction made
  **before any lease or computation**: initial ready versions were replaced to
  strengthen protocol/numerics/code cache identity. Scientific inputs and criteria
  were unchanged. Those original versions had no lease and are non-executable
  non-heads; they are excluded from the executed reuse count. Root's original
  coordinator-readiness receipt was not altered.
- [Plot provenance](report-provenance.json) is separate from solver production.
  The figure was rendered from actual saved CSV states. Artifact declarations use
  reference-only content URNs and unknown licenses remain null; public hosting and
  byte-availability projection are separate from scientific acceptance.

The worker used only contributor authority. Readiness came from the coordinator;
review requires a separate operator. At captured producer readback both Actions
were **submitted** and both Evidence records **proposed**. A subsequent reviewer
receipt may update those states without changing these historical receipts.

## Bounded independent replay

Use an isolated checkout and separate output directory. Under a 1-CPU, 4-GiB,
swap-zero, 128-task, 600-second systemd scope with numeric-library threads set to
one, load the frozen protocol and each saved pre-run Claim record, then call
`engineering.claim_reuse.compute.compute(record, protocol, case, review_output)`.
This needs NumPy/SciPy and the existing source tree, not the producer credential.
Check original artifact hashes first; compare physical profiles/metrics under the
already frozen tolerances. Timestamps/wall time make whole-result JSON byte
identity inappropriate. Running the contribution client again is deliberately
blocked by its existing-attempt guard; replay is distinct from another live lease.

Six focused input-integrity, causal-binding, redaction and cache-identity tests
passed before execution. The final audit independently checked actual persisted
records and artifacts. Neither result establishes biological validity.
claim_reuse.author_response:
# Author response to the independent fin Claim-reuse review

October 31, 2026. This is a post-review clarification. It changes no frozen
protocol, Action/Evidence record, simulation output, producer receipt or review.
The producer's original readback remains a historical submission snapshot.

I read the review at commit
`c5d4163b35aa1a65dd8700b4242f1cbc195a669c`, including its findings and
`verify-output.json`. The reviewer reports separate closed-form/FEM calculations
and author-code replays supporting the two conditional numerical verdicts.
Reading those artifacts is not another independent rerun by the author.

The reviewer recorded both Evidence records as **disputed**: scoped computation
checks passed, while empirical relevance and independent replication remained
insufficient. That decision is preserved. Mathematical agreement between two
agent processes does not provide independent biological replication, measured
fin stiffness, fluid–structure validation or organism feasibility. The Actions
remain submitted in the review handoff; no author acceptance is requested here.

| Finding | Author clarification and remaining gap |
| --- | --- |
| Copied source-only limitation | Agreed. The statement that Frontier had not executed the calculation belongs to the **historical source Claim**, not these newly executed candidate Evidence records. The saved producer receipts and outputs document the actual bounded computations. The copied text is overly conservative and misleading in this new context. It is not silently rewritten; future Evidence construction should label inherited limitations by their source and add result-specific limits separately. |
| “Mesh convergence” | Agreed. For this uniform-load/constant-EI Hermite beam case, nodal results are exact up to numerical round-off. Agreement across 16/32/64 elements supports implementation/analytic consistency here; it establishes no convergence rate. Growing round-off with refinement is retained. The off-node profile check is also a numerical comparison for this case, not a general convergence theorem. |
| Claim-mutation refusals | Agreed. The altered Record fixtures were rejected at digest validation. This demonstrates integrity refusal, not independent execution of every downstream scope check. The L³ wrong-law control is a distinct solver/model mutation and remains separately recorded. A future isolated unit test could exercise the context-consistency condition with valid, deliberately constructed fixture records and matching test pins; that would be new evidence, not a retroactive claim about these runs. |
| Candidate margins in Action payloads | Agreed. The exact 9/10 and 11/10 choices were frozen in the pre-run protocol and retained in effective inputs; the revised Action cache identity commits to their protocol bytes. They were not separate human-readable numeric Action payload fields. Future proposals should expose these values directly as well as retaining the digest. No original Action is revised after execution. |

The narrow supported result remains: two distinct bounded computations consumed
the same exact Claim version before deriving EI and executing the installed beam
solver. For the declared surrogate, the 9/10 candidate exceeded the tip/span
limit and the 11/10 candidate remained inside the declared limits. This is actual
versioned reuse and a contribution/review workflow with a retained disagreement;
it is not evidence of collective benefit, agent superiority or a calibrated fin.

No further simulation, live credentialed write, acceptance-criterion change or
review-state mutation was performed for this response. The original 56-file
producer artifact manifest continues to describe its original snapshot; this
addendum is separate from that manifest and from the reviewer's artifacts.

causal_gaps: Reporter activity shows that an element can drive expression in the tested context; it does not show that the element controls outgrowth, ECM deposition, ray geometry or fin stiffness.

The developmental-fin versus regeneration gap, scoped to the fish-fin trait bridge: PMC10211259 tests both developmental and regeneration enhancers in larval tissues, but no source read shows that any enhancer drives expression in the developing paired fin, or ties any enhancer to fin shape or stiffness.
Replicate independence of the multiome data is unconfirmed (metadata audit 1b77f81).

insect-flight.title: Redesigning insect flight
insect-flight.doc_title: 15. Redesigning insect flight: the design space
insect-flight.home_blurb: The four-winged fly is famous. What nobody measured is whether it flies.
insect-flight.nothing_attempted_note: nothing here was run in an animal.
insect-flight.studies_note: Three studies, all simulations. None is an observation, none is calibrated to a measured four-winged fly, and nothing here was run in an animal. In the venation study two of four declared controls FAIL and are reported as failing rather than repaired, so read its controls before its result.
insect-flight.goal: Ultrabithorax represses wing identity on the third thoracic segment, and losing it gives Lewis's four-winged fly — one of the best-evidenced regulatory lesions in biology. The obvious engineering question is whether more wings means more flight. This page maps every route we can source to a redesigned flight apparatus, and asks what the four-winged fly would actually do if you threw it in the air.
insect-flight.summary: The famous mutant is famous for its appearance. We could find no published measurement of free flight in a four-winged Drosophila, so the question has an answer in the literature only if you assemble it from two separate phenotypes. Doing that, and then modelling the aerodynamics and the control loop, gives a worse outcome than the picture suggests — and for a reason that has nothing to do with wing number.

answer.headline: It would fly badly, for two reasons, and neither is "four wings".
paragraphs: Start with the result that needs no biology at all. Lift scales with the second moment of wing area, so splitting one wing into two smaller ones at the same total area and aspect ratio loses more than half of it. In our blade-element model, four wings at the same total area carry 0.46 body weights — it does not leave the ground. Four wings at double the area do fly, at 1.83 body weights, but they cost twice the mass-specific mechanical power. That kills the intuitive "redistribute the area" design before any gene is named, and it falls out of geometry.

The configuration the literature actually produced is worse than either, and the reason is the first thing a designer should know. In flies homozygous for the classic allele combination, the adults have two pairs of wings, but — in the authors' own words — "the homeotically transformed T3 (HT3) has only rudimentary indirect flight muscles". The lesion transforms the epidermis; the mesoderm keeps expressing Antennapedia, which is the likely reason the flight muscle never forms. You get a wing with no engine. Modelled, that configuration carries 0.84 body weights, and it stays below one at every non-negative value of the contested fore–hind interference term, so the conclusion does not rest on choosing a convenient value for a number nobody has pinned down.

The second cost is the sensor. A haltere is a hindwing already spent on something else — a gyroscopic rate sensor — and converting it back to a wing deletes it. The model says why that matters, and the useful form of the answer is not “vision is weaker”. Sweeping the feedback delay and giving every delay the best gain available to it, no loop slower than about three wingbeats, 14 milliseconds, can meet the measured recovery from a disturbance at any gain. The haltere loop is inside that bound. The visual loop is well outside it. Vision is not too weak; it is too slow to be turned up. This is a re-derivation, not a discovery: Elzinga, Dickson and Dickinson measured “a fundamental trade-off between sensor delay and permissible feedback gain” on a dynamically scaled robotic fly in 2012, and proposed the very architecture our study assumes — “a haltere-mediated inner-loop proportional controller provides damping for slower visually mediated feedback”. Our model recovers their result in a different medium with different parameters, which is worth something as a check and nothing as a claim of priority.

A caution the page insists on: none of this says four wings are worse than two. Dragonflies have flown with four independently controlled wings for 300 million years, and their fore–hind phasing can improve efficiency rather than cost it. Remove roughly half the wing area from a moth or a butterfly and it still flies, losing acceleration but not turning radius. What makes the dipteran case different is specific to Diptera: the hindwing has already been spent, so converting it back costs a sensor and arrives without an engine.

So the route worth proposing is the one nobody has run. Transform the T3 mesoderm as well as the epidermis, and give the second wing pair an engine. Both halves are published separately — that T2 mesoderm is specified entirely by induction and expresses no selector of its own, that ectopic homeotic expression in it respecifies its muscle, and that Antennapedia persists in the transformed T3 mesoderm. The experiment is to run that in the other direction.
answer.precision_note: We found no published measurement of free-flight performance in a four-winged Drosophila. Everything above assembles two separately published phenotypes — rudimentary indirect flight muscle in the transformed segment, and haltere necessity in otherwise normal flies — plus our own model. Nobody has thrown one in the air and measured it.

chain.title: The chain across scales, and where it is not calibrated
chain.intro: From a Hox dose to a body in the air. One junction is a model whose held-out prediction lands, one is a published phenotype, one is refused, and one is a null.

links.note: The best-supported junction here. Calibrated on the Ubx arm alone, the model predicts the independently measured Antennapedia threshold to within 4.0%, against 39.2% for the switch-like variant — and both variants pass the same controls, so it is a fair comparison rather than a strawman. Stronger still, a test that needs no model: the two published thresholds sit on opposite branches of the switch, and their ordering is the one a hysteretic switch forbids.

Refused, and this is the design space's central finding. Epidermal identity follows the lesion; mesodermal identity does not, so the transformed segment gets a wing and no indirect flight muscle. The two are controlled separately and nobody has transformed both. Until someone does, 'four-winged fly' names an animal with two wings and two ornaments.

Inside the blade-element model, and the part of it that matters is geometric rather than biological: lift goes with the second moment of wing area. Same total area over four wings gives 0.46 body weights; double area gives 1.83 at twice the power. 18 of its 24 parameters are assumed, so the ratios are more trustworthy than the absolute numbers, and the model is calibrated so that wild type supports exactly body weight.

A delay bound rather than a gain comparison: no loop slower than about three wingbeats meets the measured recovery at any gain in the declared family. The same trade-off was measured on a robotic fly by Elzinga et al. in 2012, so this junction reproduces a published result rather than establishing a new one. The model recovers in 13 ms where the real fly takes under 60, so it is OPTIMISTIC about control and therefore understates the cost of deleting the sensor.

A genuine null, reported because it is the story one would otherwise tell. Four-wing recovery curves sit within 1% of two-wing ones at a 0.5% wing-mass fraction. The four-winged fly's control problem is the deleted sensor, not the added rotational inertia.

chain.verdict: The end-to-end statement — this allele gives that flight performance — is refused, because the animal it describes has never been flown. What the chain does deliver is an ordering of the obstacles: the missing engine comes first, the missing sensor second, and the added inertia not at all.

not_claimed: No fly was made, no animal was used, and no wet-lab experiment was run for this page.
There is no published measurement of free-flight performance in a four-winged Drosophila. The conclusion assembles two separately published phenotypes plus our own model.

This page does not claim that four wings are worse than two. Odonata and the hindwing-ablation literature refute that as a general statement; the claim here is specific to Diptera, where the hindwing has already been spent on a sensor.

The delay-versus-gain bound in the flight study is a re-derivation. Elzinga, Dickson and Dickinson published the same trade-off, measured on a dynamically scaled robot, in 2012, and proposed the inner-loop architecture our model assumes. Reproducing it in a different medium is a check on our model, not a new finding.

The venation study fails two of its four declared controls, including the one added to ask whether its readout had converged. Part of its quoted seed spread is convergence rather than pattern formation, and the runs were not lengthened until it passed.
18 of the flight model's 24 parameters are assumed rather than sourced. Its ratios are more trustworthy than its absolute numbers.
A threshold in a model is not a threshold in an animal.

closing.title: What this page is for

link.text: The working notes, including the sentence this page must not write

closing.text: The four-winged fly has been a textbook picture for fifty years, and the picture is of an appearance. Asking what it would do in the air turns one famous lesion into an ordered list of obstacles, two of which are published and separate and one of which is a null. Every route here carries its evidence level, a row read only at listing level says so rather than being paraphrased, and two of the controls on this page failed and say so. The useful output is not the answer but the next experiment: give the second pair an engine.

schematic.intro: One thorax, three segments, and the two things the famous lesion does not change. The routes below act at different places in this picture, and the reason the four-winged fly flies badly is that two of these places are controlled separately.
schematic.title: Where each family of routes acts on the thorax of a fly
schematic.desc: On the left, a fly's thorax in side view with its three segments labelled T1, T2 and T3. T2 carries a wing above and an indirect flight muscle inside it; T3 carries a haltere, a small club-shaped organ, above a segment whose interior is drawn empty to show it has only rudimentary flight muscle. An arrow marks the homeotic transformation that converts the T3 haltere into a second wing while leaving the muscle compartment empty. On the right, two small panels: above, a wing outline with its longitudinal veins and a bracket showing the model makes one vein too few; below, a feedback diagram in which a haltere feeds a fast loop and an eye feeds a slow one into the same wing-steering output, with a delay bound marked at three wingbeats. Six numbered pins mark where the routes act; each is named in the list under the figure.
schematic.caption: Schematic, not a measurement and not to scale.

pins.name: The Ubx switch and its enhancers
pins.note: Where appendage identity is decided, and the resolution at which this is a design problem rather than a knockout. Hox dose rather than Hox presence sets the outcome, and our model's held-out prediction lands within 4% on the graded reading.

pins.name: Wing specification in T2
pins.note: vestigial, scalloped, apterous, nubbin — the selectors that make a wing a wing. Repressing them is how T3 is kept a haltere, and de-repressing them is how the famous mutant gets its second pair.

pins.name: The indirect flight muscle
pins.note: The engine, and the reason the four-winged fly is a disappointment. Mesodermal identity is controlled separately from epidermal identity, so the transformed segment gets a wing and only rudimentary muscle. This is the route the page recommends fixing.

pins.name: The transformation itself
pins.note: What the classic allele combination actually does: it converts the T3 epidermis, leaving the mesoderm expressing Antennapedia. A wing arrives; an engine does not.

pins.name: Vein patterning
pins.note: Lateral inhibition sets vein spacing on the blade. Our model gets the spacing right to 0.07% of linear theory and the count wrong by a near-constant one vein — a boundary effect, not a scaling error. Two of its four controls fail.

pins.name: The haltere and the control loop
pins.note: A hindwing already spent on a gyroscopic rate sensor. Converting it back deletes it, and no loop slower than about three wingbeats can meet the measured recovery at any gain — so vision cannot simply be turned up to compensate.

routes.title: Insect flight: wing number, wing form, and steering
routes.note: Published perturbations and bounded proposals, grouped by the scale they act at. Every row carries its own evidence level and read levels on its sources. A row read only at listing level says NOT READ in place of a finding, rather than being paraphrased as if it reported one.
routes.nothing_attempted: None of these routes has been attempted by us.
routes.recommendation_title: If you asked us to actually do it

outcome_classes.label: More wing, or a second pair
outcome_classes.match: ^(TWO PAIRS OF WINGS|ECTOPIC WING|AN ADDITIONAL WING|FOUR WINGS|A HINDWING THAT|A SECOND PAIR|AN ECTOPIC WING|A NORMAL WING)

outcome_classes.label: Fewer wings, or none
outcome_classes.match: ^(NO WING|WINGED OR WINGLESS|A WINGLESS CASTE|LOSS OF WING|Loss of wing|LONG-WINGED OR SHORT-WINGED|THOUSANDS OF INDEPENDENT LOSSES|A WING-LENGTH)

outcome_classes.label: A different kind of wing
outcome_classes.match: ^(A HALTERE-LIKE WING|A HALTERE WITH|VEINS|A BLISTERED WING|A BIGGER haltere|A LARGER OR SMALLER BLADE|A PARTIAL|MORE OR FEWER|AN INTERMEDIATE APPENDAGE)

outcome_classes.label: Different actuation or power
outcome_classes.match: ^(SPECIFIC, PREDICTABLE CHANGES IN WING MOTION|DESYNCHRONISED|A CHANGE IN FLIGHT STABILISATION)

outcome_classes.label: Different steering, sensing or stability
outcome_classes.match: ^(LOSS OF EQUILIBRIUM|A LINEAR DECLINE|A CHANGE IN WING MOTOR|SACCADE AMPLITUDE|A HARD TRADE-OFF|DEGRADED WALKING|LOSS OF POSTURAL|HALTERE FREQUENCY|A FLY WITH NO RATE GYRO|CONTROLLED FLIGHT|STEERING|A LINEAR SUM|FOUR WINGS THAT CAN BE BETTER|A FLYING INSECT WITH|THEY STILL FLY|HALTERE REMOVAL)

routes.outcome_classes_note: Matched against the route's `predicted_phenotype` ONLY, and anchored on the capitalised phrase each one opens with. NOT against the title: a title routinely names the STARTING condition ('a segment that has no wing'), and matching it tagged six routes with the opposite of their outcome. The order matters - first match wins. Every route also carries a precomputed `outcome` field holding the result of this same matching, checked by hand route by route; if a renderer's own matching disagrees with that field, the field is right and the renderer is wrong.
routes.question: Could you redesign an insect's flight apparatus - and if you added wings, would it fly better?
routes.short_answer: The experiment has been done since 1978 and the answer is no, for two independent reasons that the literature separates cleanly: the second pair of wings has almost no engine, and the organ you spent to get it was a rate gyroscope. Neither of those is a general law about four wings - dragonflies have had four independently controlled wings for 300 million years - and the page is organised around what makes the dipteran case different.

scales.label: Molecular · cis-regulatory
scales.blurb: Change non-coding DNA and leave every protein intact. This is the layer at which a Hox gene actually acts - Ubx does not build a haltere, it re-reads the wing's own enhancers - and it is the layer at which evolution has repeatedly changed appendage identity without changing the appendage toolkit.

scales.label: Gene · selectors and identity
scales.blurb: Delete or force the selector proteins themselves. The phenotypes here are the strongest and the oldest in the literature; Lewis's four-winged fly is one of them. They are also the ones that transform the SKIN of a segment and leave its muscle behind, which is the whole problem with the four-winged design.

scales.label: Network · wing specification
scales.blurb: The signalling circuit that decides there will be a wing at all, and how big: Wingless, Notch/Serrate/Delta, Dpp and the Vestigial-Scalloped selector complex. Turning these knobs gives you more wing or less wing, rarely a different KIND of wing.

scales.label: Pattern · venation and blade
scales.blurb: What the wing membrane is actually made of. Veins carry the haemolymph, the tracheae and the campaniform sensilla, and they set the blade's bending stiffness, so a venation change is a structural change and a sensory change at the same time.

scales.label: Actuator · muscle and hinge
scales.blurb: The engine and the gearbox. A wing is useless without the indirect flight muscle that drives the thorax and the hinge sclerites that convert thoracic oscillation into a stroke. This scale is where the four-winged fly fails, and almost nobody asking for a second pair of wings is thinking about it.

scales.label: Sensor · haltere and campaniform system
scales.blurb: The haltere is the hindwing, reduced to a club and rebuilt as a rate gyroscope. Everything that converts a hindwing into a wing deletes it. This scale exists on the page because the obvious design intuition - more wings, better flight - ignores the organ it is proposing to spend.

scales.label: Neural · steering and control
scales.blurb: The loop that closes between sensor and actuator, in under a wingbeat. It is also the layer at which insect flight has already been redesigned by engineers, by implanting stimulators rather than by changing any gene.

scales.label: Organism · plasticity and morph
scales.blurb: Several insects already switch their own wings on and off within a single genome, on an environmental cue. If you want a wing-number change that is reversible and non-lethal, this is the only scale where nature has already solved it.

scales.label: Comparative · other orders
scales.blurb: Four independently controlled wings (Odonata), coupled fore- and hindwings (Lepidoptera), halteres on the WRONG segment (Strepsiptera), and thousands of independent losses of flight. These are the experiments evolution has already run.

routes.title: Disable the Ubx-bound enhancers that build a haltere, leaving Ubx protein intact
routes.intervention: Delete or mutate the Ubx-occupied regulatory elements at haltere-specific targets identified by genome-wide occupancy, one target at a time, rather than removing Ubx itself.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A PARTIAL wing-ward transformation of the haltere, target by target, rather than the whole-appendage switch a Ubx null gives. Which traits move depends on which target you hit: Ubx acts on genes at several levels of the wing-patterning hierarchy at once, so no single enhancer carries the whole identity.
routes.mechanism: Ubx is a transcription factor; the haltere is what its targets build. Occupancy maps give the candidate elements, and Ubx's target set CHANGES between stages of haltere morphogenesis, so the same element deleted at a different time is a different experiment.
routes.reversibility: Not reversible in the animal: a germline sequence change. Reversible at the design stage, because each element is independent of the others.
routes.lethality_risk: Low. Ubx protein is untouched, so the segmental and abdominal functions that make a Ubx null lethal are intact.
routes.difficulty: High. The occupancy maps give hundreds of candidates and no map says which are REQUIRED; each one is its own allele.

evidence.cite: Slattery M et al. 2011, PLoS One 6:e14686, 'Genome-wide tissue-specific occupancy of the Hox protein Ultrabithorax and Hox cofactor Homothorax in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: Genome-wide, tissue-specific occupancy of Ubx and its cofactor Homothorax in Drosophila, motivated explicitly by the question of 'what target genes Ubx regulates to generate these adult structures'.

evidence.cite: Pavlopoulos A et al. 2011, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 108:2855-60, 'Hox gene Ultrabithorax regulates distinct sets of target genes at successive stages of Drosophila haltere morphogenesis'
evidence.finding: Ubx 'regulates distinct sets of target genes at successive stages of Drosophila haltere morphogenesis' - so the target list is a function of developmental time, not a fixed set.

evidence.cite: Weatherbee SD et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:1474-82, 'Ultrabithorax regulates genes at several levels of the wing-patterning hierarchy to shape the development of the Drosophila haltere'
evidence.finding: Ubx 'regulates genes at several levels of the wing-patterning hierarchy'; it represses Wingless and a subset of Wg- and Dpp-activated genes such as spalt-related.

routes.title: Titrate Ubx dose rather than removing it, and ask for an intermediate appendage
routes.intervention: Reduce Ubx protein in the T3 pouch in graded steps - by allelic series, RNAi titration or degron - instead of removing it.
routes.predicted_phenotype: AN INTERMEDIATE APPENDAGE, if the decision is a dial. Wing-like traits appear once Ubx falls to about 39% of its endogenous level, and the approach to that point is the question: a graded appendage or a switch. Our own model (study 1) fits the graded reading and, calibrated on the Ubx arm alone, predicts the independently measured Antp threshold to within 4.0%; the switch-like variant misses it by 39.2%. (An earlier, stale copy of that study reported the gap as a factor of 40; re-running its own code showed the switch-like variant passes the same controls, which makes this a fair comparison and a smaller one.) The sharper test needs no model at all: the two published thresholds sit on OPPOSITE branches of the switch, so their ordering tests hysteresis directly, and under both protein-ratio measurements the ordering is the one a hysteretic switch forbids - under the GFP ratio the two doses are within 4% of each other, i.e. effectively a single threshold.
routes.mechanism: Hox dose, not Hox presence, sets appendage identity. The wing selector Vestigial-Scalloped is repressed by Ubx, and the decision is where that repression crosses the selector's own threshold.
routes.reversibility: Fully reversible if done with a degron or inducible RNAi; this is the most reversible route on the page at the gene scale.
routes.lethality_risk: Low if restricted to the T3 disc.
routes.difficulty: Moderate. The reagents exist; the hard part is measuring the dose rather than assuming it.

evidence.cite: Paul R et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:2892, 'Hox dosage contributes to flight appendage morphology in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: Full text read (PMC8129201, fetched this session). 'characteristic wing-like phenotypic traits (including veins, hairs organization, and flattening) eventually appeared when the level decreased to 39% of endogenous Ubx'; the paper gives that as 2.5 times lower than endogenous Ubx. And, decisively for study 1's model comparison: 'In both cases, intermediate levels led to intermediary phenotypes' - which is the graded reading, observed directly, independently of any model.

routes.title: Change organ SIZE without changing organ identity, through the Ubx-dally-Dpp axis
routes.intervention: Restore Dpp transcription and mobility in the haltere pouch by de-repressing dally and lowering thickveins, without touching Ubx's identity targets.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A BIGGER haltere that is still a haltere. The haltere ends larval life with roughly fivefold fewer cells than the wing, and this is the axis that sets that number - so this route separates 'how large' from 'what kind', which is exactly the distinction a wing-number redesign keeps conflating.
routes.mechanism: Ubx limits haltere size by restricting both the transcription and the mobility of Dpp, raising the receptor thickveins and, with engrailed, repressing the glypican dally in the posterior compartment.
routes.reversibility: Depends on the reagent; a conditional allele makes it reversible, a deletion does not.
routes.lethality_risk: Low to moderate. Dpp is used everywhere, so the restriction to the haltere pouch is the whole safety argument.
routes.difficulty: Moderate.

evidence.cite: Crickmore MA et al. 2006, Science 313:63-8, 'Hox control of organ size by regulation of morphogen production and mobility'
evidence.finding: Ubx 'controls haltere size by restricting both the transcription and the mobility of the morphogen Decapentaplegic (Dpp)' and 'restricts Dpp's distribution in the haltere by increasing the amounts of the Dpp receptor, thickveins'. By the end of larval development the haltere has 'approximately fivefold fewer cells than the wing'.

evidence.cite: Crickmore MA et al. 2007, Development 134:327-34, 'Hox control of morphogen mobility and organ development through regulation of glypican expression'
evidence.finding: Ubx 'modulates morphogen signaling in the haltere through transcriptional regulation of the glypican dally' and, with engrailed, represses dally in the posterior compartment.

evidence.cite: Han C et al. 2005, Development 132:667-79, 'Drosophila glypicans Dally and Dally-like shape the extracellular Wingless morphogen gradient in the wing disc'
evidence.finding: Dally and Dally-like 'are essential and have different roles in Wg gradient formation' in the wing disc - the same glypican machinery, on the other morphogen.

routes.title: Drive the vestigial quadrant enhancer in a segment that has no wing
routes.intervention: Place the vestigial boundary and quadrant enhancers under ectopic control, so that the wing selector is switched on where the two normal signals do not meet.
routes.predicted_phenotype: ECTOPIC WING TISSUE growing out of whatever structure you switched it on in. In Drosophila, vestigial is 'sufficient to induce outgrowths of wing tissue from eyes, legs and antennae' - which is the cleanest demonstration on this page that wing number is not a body-plan constant.
routes.mechanism: vestigial integrates two separate positional signals through two separate enhancers: Notch at the dorsoventral organiser first, then Dpp plus a signal from that organiser in the blade. Bypassing the integration is what makes the outgrowth ectopic.
routes.reversibility: Reversible at the design stage if driven by an inducible system; the outgrowth itself is not.
routes.lethality_risk: Moderate. Wing tissue on an eye or a leg is a welfare and viability problem in its own right.
routes.difficulty: Low. This is a classic, published manipulation.

evidence.cite: Kim J et al. 1996, Nature 382:133-8, 'Integration of positional signals and regulation of wing formation and identity by Drosophila vestigial gene'
evidence.finding: vestigial 'is selectively required for wing-cell proliferation, and is sufficient to induce outgrowths of wing tissue from eyes, legs and antennae'. 'Different signals activate separate enhancers': Notch at the dorsal/ventral organizer, then decapentaplegic plus a signal from that organizer in the blade.

evidence.cite: Williams JA et al. 1994, Nature 368:299-305, 'Organization of wing formation and induction of a wing-patterning gene at the dorsal/ventral compartment boundary'
evidence.finding: NOT READ. The PubMed record for this paper resolves and its title and journal are as cited; we have read none of its results and make no claim from it beyond what its title states.

routes.title: The four-winged fly: remove Ubx function from T3
routes.intervention: Combine the classical bithorax-complex alleles - anterobithorax, bithorax, postbithorax - so that T3 is transformed towards T2.
routes.predicted_phenotype: TWO PAIRS OF WINGS, and a fly that is worse at flying than it was - for two reasons that are NOT equally well evidenced, and the page says which is which. The strong one: the transformed T3 has 'only rudimentary indirect flight muscles'. The second pair has no engine. That is direct, quoted, unambiguous insect phenotype. The weaker one: the halteres are gone with it, and the sensory cost of that is real but GRADED, task-dependent and clade-dependent rather than a flat failure - see the sensor scale. So the honest answer is that the swap costs an actuator outright and a sensor partially, to buy a surface.
routes.mechanism: Ubx represses wing identity in T3; removing it lets the T3 disc build a wing. The muscle does not follow, and Fernandes et al. say precisely which step breaks, which is what makes this a design problem rather than a curiosity. Their decomposition: the segmental identity of the EPIDERMIS determines the number of myoblasts on the larval discs and the pattern of their migration during metamorphosis - so those follow the transformation. The segmental identity of the MESODERM is what is crucial for the FUSION of myoblasts into indirect flight muscle, and influences the branching of motor innervation - and the mesoderm is not transformed, because Antp keeps being expressed there. Ectodermal information and autonomous mesodermal homeotic function are BOTH required. So the four-winged fly has the right number of myoblasts, delivered to the right place, that then fail to fuse.
routes.reversibility: Not reversible in the animal. The classical alleles are germline.
routes.lethality_risk: Moderate. The flies are viable; flight is not.
routes.difficulty: Low. These stocks are nearly fifty years old.

evidence.cite: Lewis EB et al. 1978, Nature 276:565-70, 'A gene complex controlling segmentation in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: The bithorax complex 'contains a minimum of eight genes that seem to code for substances controlling levels of thoracic and abdominal development'; repression of at least four is controlled by cis-regulatory elements.

evidence.cite: Fernandes J et al. 1994, Curr Biol 4:957-64, 'Muscle development in the four-winged Drosophila and the role of the Ultrabithorax gene'
evidence.finding: In flies homozygous for anterobithorax, bithorax3 and postbithorax, 'The adults have two pairs of wings, but the homeotically transformed T3 (HT3) has only rudimentary indirect flight muscles'. The decomposition is theirs: 'the segmental identity of the epidermis determines the segment-specific pattern and number of myoblasts on the larval discs, and the pattern of their migration during metamorphosis. The segmental identity of the mesoderm, however, is crucial for the fusion of myoblasts to form indirect flight muscles, and also influences the branching pattern of innervation of indirect flight muscles.' Their conclusion: 'Segmental information expressed in the ectoderm, and the autonomous function of hom[eotic selector genes in the mesoderm]' are both required.

evidence.cite: Roy S et al. 1997, Curr Biol 7:222-7, 'Muscles in the Drosophila second thoracic segment are patterned independently of autonomous homeotic gene function'
evidence.finding: 'Antp continues to be expressed in the mesoderm of the homeotically transformed third thoracic segment in the four-winged fly', which the authors 'suggest ... is a likely reason for the failure of flight muscle development in the transformed segment'.

evidence.cite: Mureli S et al. 2015, J Exp Biol 218:2528-37, 'Haltere mechanosensory influence on tethered flight behavior in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: CITED FOR WHAT IT MEASURED, NOT FOR ITS OPENING PREMISE. The sentence 'Haltere input is necessary for free flight' is this abstract's second sentence and is background - it is there to explain why the experiments are TETHERED ('making it difficult to study the effects of haltere ablation under natural flight conditions'). Their own findings are narrower and partly cut the other way: 'Haltere removal does not affect the flies' ability to flap or steer their wings', and 'intact halteres are not strictly necessary for visually guided wing-steering responses'. What they do show is that haltereless flies 'cannot stabilize a wide-field stimulus as accurately as intact flies can' while they 'fixate figures with the same acuity as intact flies'. See the route sen-haltere-ablation, which carries this in full.

routes.title: Run it backwards: force Ubx in T2 and convert the wing into a haltere
routes.intervention: Express Ubx ectopically in the wing pouch.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A HALTERE-LIKE WING: Wingless signalling and a subset of Wg- and Dpp-activated genes such as spalt-related are repressed, and the blade loses the wing's margin bristles and its veins. A fly with four halteres and no wings does not fly at all, which is the other end of the same axis and is worth putting on the page beside the four-winged one.
routes.mechanism: Ubx acts at several levels of the wing-patterning hierarchy simultaneously, so forcing it in T2 removes the wing programme rather than editing it.
routes.lethality_risk: High for flight; the animal survives, the behaviour does not.
routes.difficulty: Low.

evidence.cite: Weatherbee SD et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:1474-82, 'Ultrabithorax regulates genes at several levels of the wing-patterning hierarchy to shape the development of the Drosophila haltere'
evidence.finding: 'Ubx represses the expression of the Wingless (Wg) signaling protein and a subset of Wg- and Decapentaplegic-activated genes such as spalt-relat'[ed]. Ubx acts on the wing programme at several levels at once, which is why forcing it in T2 removes that programme rather than editing it. NOTE: the description of a haltere as lacking the wing's margin bristles and veins is Pallavi & Shashidhara's (PMID 16815386), where it is cited; an earlier draft attributed it to this paper, and the quote checker caught it.

evidence.cite: Mohit P et al. 2006, Dev Biol 291:356-67, 'Modulation of AP and DV signaling pathways by the homeotic gene Ultrabithorax during haltere development in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: Microarray analysis of Ubx targets during haltere specification: 'down-regulation of both anterior-posterior and dorso-ventral signaling is critical for haltere fate specification'.

routes.title: Use Antennapedia instead of Ubx, at high dose, to make a wing haltere-like
routes.intervention: Over-express Antp in the wing pouch and raise the dose until the appendage changes.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A HALTERE-LIKE WING at around 490% of endogenous Antp. That threshold is the quantitative test on this page: a Hox dose model calibrated on the Ubx arm alone predicts it, so the two Hox proteins are acting as one repressive 'dose' on one selector rather than as two qualitatively different instructions.
routes.mechanism: Antp and Ubx both repress the Vg-Sd wing selector; Antp is the weaker repressor and is present at roughly a tenth to a twentieth of Ubx's endogenous level, so a large over-expression is needed to reach the same repression.
routes.lethality_risk: Moderate; ectopic Antp is not benign outside the pouch.
routes.difficulty: Moderate: the experiment is only meaningful if the dose is measured, and the two published measurements of the Ubx:Antp ratio in the SAME paper disagree by nearly twofold.

evidence.cite: Paul R et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:2892, 'Hox dosage contributes to flight appendage morphology in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: Full text read (PMC8129201). 'the wing resembled a haltere in terms of size, shape, and hairs organization when the expression level corresponded to 490% of endogenous Antp'; the paper gives that as five times higher than endogenous Antp. On the Ubx:Antp ratio the paper reports TWO numbers: 'Ubx was 18.5 times more strongly expressed than Antp' by antibody, and 'Ubx expression levels were 10.5 times higher than Antp levels' by matched GFP. It does not leave them in conflict - it attributes the gap to affinity, concluding 'the Antp antibody is 1.85 times less affine' - so the GFP number is the paper's own preferred measurement. Study 1 calibrated both and its GFP arm is the one that predicts the held-out Antp threshold to 4%.

routes.title: Delete vestigial and lose the wing entirely
routes.intervention: Null or wing-specific regulatory mutation of vestigial.
routes.predicted_phenotype: NO WING. vestigial is selectively required for wing-cell proliferation; without it the blade does not grow. This is the negative control for the whole page: it shows the wing is a selector-defined organ, so wing NUMBER is a question about where the selector is switched on.
routes.mechanism: Vestigial partners Scalloped to form the wing selector; Vg binding switches Sd's DNA-target selectivity, so without Vg the same Sd protein reads a different set of sites.
routes.lethality_risk: Low. Wingless flies are viable in the laboratory.
routes.difficulty: Low.

evidence.cite: Kim J et al. 1996, Nature 382:133-8, 'Integration of positional signals and regulation of wing formation and identity by Drosophila vestigial gene'
evidence.finding: vestigial 'is selectively required for wing-cell proliferation'.

evidence.cite: Halder G et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3900-9, 'The Vestigial and Scalloped proteins act together to directly regulate wing-specific gene expression in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: Vestigial 'requires the function of the Scalloped protein ... to directly activate the expression of genes involved in wing morphogenesis'.

evidence.cite: Halder G et al. 2001, Development 128:3295-305, 'Binding of the Vestigial co-factor switches the DNA-target selectivity of the Scalloped selector protein'
evidence.finding: 'Binding of Vestigial to Scalloped switches the DNA-binding selectivity of Scalloped' - the selector's specificity is made by the partnership, not by either protein.

evidence.cite: Simmonds AJ et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3815-20, 'Molecular interactions between Vestigial and Scalloped promote wing formation in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: NOT READ. The PubMed record for this paper resolves and its title and journal are as cited; we have read none of its results and make no claim from it beyond what its title states.

routes.title: Ask what vestigial does in a beetle, where one of the segments is already wingless
routes.intervention: RNAi against vestigial in Tribolium castaneum and in ladybird beetles.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Loss of wing tissue, AND the discovery that the 'wingless' first thoracic segment of a beetle contains two groups of vg-dependent tissues. That matters for a redesign: a segment with no wing is not necessarily a segment with no wing PROGRAMME, so the cheapest place to add a wing may be a segment that already has the latent tissue.
routes.mechanism: vg is a conserved wing gene across insects; ectopic ladybird vg induces wing-like tissue in Drosophila antennae and legs, so the selector is interchangeable across 300 million years.
routes.reversibility: RNAi is transient, so this is among the more reversible routes.
routes.lethality_risk: Low to moderate; the ladybird work found an unexpected requirement in pupal ecdysis, which is a lethality route nobody predicted from the wing phenotype.
routes.difficulty: Moderate.

evidence.cite: Clark-Hachtel CM et al. 2013, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 110:16951-6, 'Insights into insect wing origin provided by functional analysis of vestigial in the red flour beetle, Tribolium castaneum'
evidence.finding: 'Our investigation in Tribolium (Coleoptera) has revealed that, despite the well-accepted view of vg as an essential wing gene, there are two groups of vg-dependent tissues in the "wingless" first thoracic segment'.

routes.title: Remove the dorsoventral organiser with apterous and get no wing at all
routes.intervention: Loss of apterous function in the wing disc.
routes.predicted_phenotype: NO WING. apterous specifies dorsal identity and creates the dorsoventral compartment boundary; the organiser at that boundary is what induces the blade. The failure mode is instructive for a designer: you cannot add a wing by adding wing tissue, you add it by creating a BOUNDARY.
routes.mechanism: Dorsal cells expressing apterous meet ventral cells; the interaction at the interface drives wing development.
routes.lethality_risk: Low.
routes.difficulty: Low.

evidence.cite: Diaz-Benjumea FJ et al. 1993, Cell 75:741-52, 'Interaction between dorsal and ventral cells in the imaginal disc directs wing development in Drosophila'
evidence.finding: 'spatially localized expression of the homeobox gene apterous (ap) specifies the identity of dorsal cells in the wing'; the lineage-restriction boundary 'coincides with the limit of the domain' of ap expression.

routes.title: Attack the hinge rather than the blade, with nubbin
routes.intervention: Wing-disc-specific regulatory mutations of nubbin.
routes.predicted_phenotype: LOSS OF WING STRUCTURES with a localised requirement in the wing HINGE, not the blade. A design that adds wings has to articulate them, and this is the gene that says the hinge is its own growth-control centre rather than the proximal end of the blade's.
routes.mechanism: nubbin encodes a POU-domain transcription factor; mosaic analysis localises its requirement to the hinge, implying a proximal-distal organiser additional to the AP and DV ones.
routes.lethality_risk: Low.
routes.difficulty: Low.

evidence.cite: Ng M et al. 1995, Development 121:589-99, 'Nubbin encodes a POU-domain protein required for proximal-distal patterning in the Drosophila wing'
evidence.finding: 'Regulatory mutants which selectively remove nubbin expression from wing imaginal discs lead to loss of wing structures'; mosaics suggest 'a localized requirement for nubbin activity in the wing hinge' and 'a novel proximal-distal growth control center in the wing hinge'.

routes.title: Change hindwing identity in an insect whose hindwing is still a wing
routes.intervention: Perturb Ubx function in butterfly hindwings.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A HINDWING THAT LOOKS MORE LIKE A FOREWING, including its colour pattern. This is the route that separates 'Ubx makes a haltere' from 'Ubx makes a hindwing DIFFERENT': in Lepidoptera the same gene differentiates two flying wings rather than destroying one, which is the existence proof that a four-winged redesign is reachable without losing an aerofoil.
routes.mechanism: Hox genes are transcription factors, so appendage diversity can evolve by changing which targets they regulate rather than by changing the Hox gene itself.
routes.lethality_risk: Unknown in butterflies.
routes.difficulty: High: the genetic toolkit is far thinner than Drosophila's.

evidence.cite: Weatherbee SD et al. 1999, Curr Biol 9:109-15, 'Ultrabithorax function in butterfly wings and the evolution of insect wing patterns'

evidence.cite: Tomoyasu Y et al. 2017, Curr Opin Insect Sci 19:8-15, 'Ultrabithorax and the evolution of insect forewing/hindwing differentiation'

routes.title: Specify an extra wing field with localised Wingless
routes.intervention: Drive wingless expression ectopically in the second instar, when the wing/body-wall subdivision is made.
routes.predicted_phenotype: AN ADDITIONAL WING FIELD, if the timing is right. Wing specification is a second-instar event, so this route has a window rather than a dose, which is the kind of knob that makes a design reproducible.
routes.mechanism: Localised Wingless protein specifies the wing compartment of the disc, downstream of the apterous-dependent DV subdivision.
routes.lethality_risk: Moderate: wingless is pleiotropic.
routes.difficulty: Moderate; the timing is the hard part.

evidence.cite: Ng M et al. 1996, Nature 381:316-8, 'Specification of the wing by localized expression of wingless protein'
evidence.finding: 'A third major subdivision of the wing disc into wing and body-wall compartments also occurs in the second instar', specified by localised Wingless.

routes.title: Build the organiser from scratch with Notch, Serrate and Delta
routes.intervention: Create an ectopic Notch-activation stripe, by juxtaposing Serrate- and Delta-expressing cells, in a disc with no wing.
routes.predicted_phenotype: AN ECTOPIC WING MARGIN and the outgrowth that follows it. Serrate signals ventrally-to-dorsally and Delta dorsally-to-ventrally, so a designer has two complementary ligands and can place the boundary rather than inherit it.
routes.mechanism: Notch activation at the DV interface turns on the vestigial boundary enhancer, which starts the blade.
routes.lethality_risk: High. Notch is used in nearly every tissue and ectopic activation is oncogenic in many of them.
routes.difficulty: Moderate.

routes.title: Reshape the wing by reshaping the Dpp gradient
routes.intervention: Alter Dpp production, receptor level or glypican availability to change the gradient's range.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A LARGER OR SMALLER BLADE with its target genes re-positioned: optomotor-blind and spalt are activated at different distances from the source, so moving the gradient moves the landmarks the venation is built on. This is the knob that changes wing AREA, which study 3 shows is the only aerodynamically profitable thing about adding wings in the first place.
routes.mechanism: Dpp acts directly and at long range; receptor levels themselves shape the gradient, so the tissue is not a passive medium.
routes.lethality_risk: Moderate.
routes.difficulty: Low to moderate.

routes.title: Replace the wing selector's co-factor with its human ortholog
routes.intervention: Substitute TONDU, the human relative of Vestigial, for Vg function in Drosophila wing formation.
routes.predicted_phenotype: A NORMAL WING, built with a human protein in place of the fly's own. TONDU 'substitutes for Vg function in wing formation'. For a design space this is the load-bearing fact: the wing selector is a module with an interface, and the interface has survived the whole bilaterian radiation, so a redesign can swap parts rather than rebuild them.
routes.mechanism: TONDU interacts with vertebrate TEF factors, the vertebrate relatives of Scalloped, and the Vg-Sd interface is conserved well enough for the substitution to work in vivo.
routes.lethality_risk: Low.
routes.difficulty: Low; it is done.
