recommendation.Why this one: It is the only body plan in this whole space that has been computationally designed, physically built, and then MEASURED on external material moved rather than on self-locomotion. Sculpting progenitors into an asymmetric semitorus with a narrow mouth raised offspring diameter by 149% and replication rounds by 250% over spherical progenitors, because the mouth captures, transports and aggregates loose cells. It is also cilia-driven, so it never has to solve the actuation problem that kills most of this page's alternatives.
recommendation.What it buys you that a gait does not: A concave mouth converts locomotion into gathering through GEOMETRY. It needs no per-region phase control, no actuator timing, and no contractile tissue graft — none of which exist in a controllable form in any living construct today. The construct just has to move; the shape does the work.
recommendation.The gait question is the wrong question,: The published six-gait comparison asks which spatial actuation phase pattern moves a soft body furthest. In the regime a real millimetre-scale construct occupies — Reynolds number below 0.1 — five of those six patterns produce EXACTLY ZERO net displacement, because they assign only the phases 0 and pi and so retrace their own stroke. The live design question is not 'which gait ranks highest' but 'is this gait non-reciprocal at all', which is a yes/no test you can run on paper in a minute.
recommendation.What to build next, in order: 1. Replicate the semitorus and measure particle clearance with a declared metric, not as a side effect. 2. Apply the rank test to any proposed actuation pattern before simulating it. 3. If you simulate, put buoyancy and drag in — Kriegman et al. already found and fixed this failure once, and the artifact we re-examined uses the physics they abandoned. 4. Evolve the ARENA (coll-evolve-the-terrain): it is the cheapest unexploited lever here and needs no new biology.
recommendation.The honest commercial position: For most mechanical tasks at this scale a magnetically or acoustically driven synthetic device wins today on steering, force, speed and reliability, and a synthetic swarm has already been shown capturing bacteria and microplastics on the fly with a retrieval story. The living construct's case rests on four narrow axes and should be argued only on those: self-repair, biodegradation and a yolk-limited lifespan as built-in containment, patient-derived immunological self (anthrobots), and kinematic self-replication. Nothing else on the comparator scale offers any of them.
recommendation.Runner-up: cell-ciliabot-building-blocks — placing cilia-inactive modules to pattern thrust by construction is gait design done with tissue instead of with timing, and it is the most manufacturable idea on this page.

welfare.Animal use: The Xenopus routes require fertilised Xenopus laevis eggs and embryos harvested at blastula stage. The source papers record institutional approval: Kriegman et al. 2020 under Tufts IACUC protocol M2017-53, Kriegman et al. 2021 under M2020-35. Shaping is subtractive surgery — microcautery with a 13 um wire electrode — performed on tissue explanted before a nervous system exists.
welfare.The anthrobot route avoids animals entir: Anthrobots are built from adult human lung epithelial cells and need no animal, no embryo and no genetic editing. If a programme can be run on that substrate, the animal-use question largely disappears. This is a substantive welfare argument for the human route and not only a commercial one.
welfare.Moral status of the constructs themselve: These constructs have no nervous system and are not sentient on any account we are aware of. They are nonetheless novel self-organising entities with behaviours absent from the donor organism, and the field itself has raised the question rather than dismissed it. We flag it and do not resolve it.
welfare.Containment: Lifespan is bounded by maternally provided yolk at 10–14 days with no feeding, replication halts after 2–4 rounds on its own, and the genome is unmodified in the baseline routes — so there is no heritable engineered material to escape. Two caveats we will not paper over: the contractile-gait route DOES inject mRNA (Notch ICD and a lineage tracer), so a designed-gait construct is not wild-type in the sense the containment argument assumes; and the AI-designed shape that makes replication useful is the same knob that makes it halt later.
welfare.What this page does not address: Any in vivo deployment. Every route here is a dish, a culture or a simulation. Delivery, biodistribution, immune response in a real body and environmental release are all out of scope and none of our studies bear on them.

limitations: Our three studies are SIMULATIONS. No organism, tissue or cell was measured for this page. Every mechanical parameter in them is marked assumed, not sourced, and the same is true of the published simulations they re-examine — Kriegman et al. 2021 state their voxel material properties were 'manually tuned to allow for the largest stable time step of numerical integration'.

The scallop-theorem result applies cleanly to a FREE SWIMMER. A xenobot crawling on a dish bottom, negatively buoyant with its ventral surface in contact, is not one: contact friction is not Stokes drag and is outside the theorem's assumptions, so a reciprocal gait can rectify against a surface. The defensible claim is that the published ranking is void for a free or near-neutrally-buoyant construct, and that for a crawler its magnitudes come from an object 3.8 orders of magnitude away in Reynolds number.

Cilia-driven propulsion is not body-deformation swimming, and most published constructs are cilia-driven. The scallop theorem still constrains the cilium's own stroke, but a surface-thrust machine has no body gait for our analysis to rank. Our regime result therefore bears directly on the 2020 cardiac-driven constructs and only indirectly on the 2021 cilia-driven ones.

Our Stokes swimmer is a Rotne-Prager-Yamakawa bead model over shapes from a quasi-static central-force spring lattice. That lattice obeys the Cauchy relations, so its Poisson ratio is a property of the spring topology rather than an input: we measure 0.20 against the artifact's 0.35, and its axial and bending effective moduli differ by about a factor of two. We use it only to generate a shape, and we report that the Stokes ranking shifts by under 1% across a 4x change in its stiffness ratio.

The five reciprocal gaits do not come back as literally zero but as 1e-7 to 1e-8 body lengths per cycle, which is the numerical residue of an iterative shape solve. We establish that by refinement rather than assertion — tightening the solve drops those values by four orders while the travelling wave holds to four significant figures — and their relative order must not be read as a ranking.

The cargo and swarm studies are in the dry-friction regime, matching the artifact they extend, NOT the viscous regime our own first study says the real object occupies. They answer 'does the best self-mover also push best' within that model and nowhere else.
Our swarm has no sensing, no communication and no differentiated roles, and every member runs the same gait. Its failure to aggregate is a statement about that swarm, not about swarms.

Read-levels are stated per source and most are 'listing' — citation record retrieved and verified from PubMed, abstract not read by us. Only Kriegman et al. 2020 and 2021 were read in full text. Four physics citations (Purcell 1977, Najafi & Golestanian 2004, Lauga 2007, Lauga & Powers 2009) are not indexed in PubMed and are labelled search-summary: their volume, page and DOI details were NOT independently verified by us.

Scope of the negative on the application question: searching PubMed and Consensus for a xenobot or anthrobot deliberately transporting a defined external cargo found nothing. What exists is debris and particle AGGREGATION as a reported side effect of locomotion, plus object transport in silico only. bioRxiv was not searched by keyword.

voxcraft-sim, the GPU engine this literature actually uses, does NOT build at its pin against a modern toolkit. We ran the probe on an NVIDIA L40S in nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04: both arms configured cleanly and both failed to compile, because the code calls cudaDeviceSynchronize() from __device__ functions (removed in CUDA 12, seven sites) and because nvcc cannot compile Boost.Asio's trait machinery reached through boost::process. No cross-engine comparison is offered anywhere here. We tested one toolkit on one platform; the pinned CUDA 10.2 route was not attempted. Receipt: data/voxcraft-probe.json.

scales.label: Molecular · adhesion, cilia and contractility
scales.blurb: What the cells are told to become. At this scale you choose whether the construct will have a propulsion system at all, and which one.

scales.label: Cell · sourcing and power source
scales.blurb: Which cells, from which organism, driven by what. The fork between ciliary surface thrust and contractile body deformation is made here, and it decides whether a gait model is even the right abstraction.

scales.label: Tissue · shape imposition and self-assembly
scales.blurb: How a designed geometry gets into a living object. Every shape on this page has to survive a 100 um minimum feature size and an hour of healing.

scales.label: Body plan · geometry and actuation pattern
scales.blurb: The design variables the published optimisation loop actually searches. This is where our three studies push hardest.

scales.label: Fluid · the regime the construct actually lives in
scales.blurb: A millimetre-scale construct in water sits at Reynolds number well below 1. That single number decides which gaits can work at all, and it is the scale most of this literature's simulations are not in.

scales.label: Design loop · search and sim-to-real transfer
scales.blurb: The pipeline that turns a goal into a built organism — and the place where this page's own subject, the gap between the simulator and the dish, lives.

scales.blurb: What changes when there is more than one. Including the one published result where constructs demonstrably rearrange their environment.

studies.title: The gait ranking is from the wrong physics
studies.question: A real millimetre-scale construct moves through water at a Reynolds number far below 1. The published gait comparison is dry friction on a floor under gravity, with inertia. Does its ranking of six actuation patterns transfer to the regime the real object occupies?
studies.summary: No, and the failure is qualitative rather than a reordering. Computed from the sizes and speeds the papers themselves report, anthrobots sit at Re = 1.5e-4 to 2.5e-2 and a nominal 1 mm xenobot at Re = 0.0996; the simulated artifact's own body, at its own size and speed, would be at Re = 643 in water, 3.8 orders of magnitude away. Five of the six published patterns assign only the phases 0 and pi, so the whole body is driven by one scalar in time and the stroke retraces itself: they are time-reciprocal, and Purcell's scallop theorem makes their net displacement exactly zero at low Reynolds number. A Rotne-Prager-Yamakawa bead-model Stokes swimmer confirms it, with the travelling wave at 0.034 body lengths per cycle and every other pattern at the numerical floor. The weakness is the one the page must not hide: this applies cleanly to a FREE SWIMMER, and a xenobot crawling on a dish with its ventral surface in contact is not one, because surface friction is not Stokes drag and sits outside the theorem's assumptions. Separately, most published constructs are cilia-driven, and cilia are surface thrust rather than a body gait, so this bears directly on the 2020 cardiac-driven constructs and only indirectly on the rest.

predeclared_questions: Q1 Reynolds number of the real construct vs the simulated object
Q2 which of the six gaits are time-reciprocal
Q3 does the dry-friction ranking survive the regime change (predeclared: NO)
Q4 is the quasi-static assumption satisfied (declared gate tau/T <= 1e-2)

reynolds_map.definition: Re = rho * U * L / mu, translational Reynolds number

simulated_object_regime.what: the voxel-actuation artifact's body, at ITS OWN simulated size and speed, IF it were in water
simulated_object_regime.caveat: the artifact has NO fluid. It is dry Coulomb friction on a rigid floor plus a numerical absolute-frame damping term. This Re is a scale comparison, not a property of that simulation.
simulated_object_regime.oscillatory_definition: Re_omega = rho * omega * L^2 / mu, the frequency Reynolds number used by Lauga 2007 for reciprocal-stroke breakdown
simulated_object_regime.speed_definition: U is PATH LENGTH divided by the measurement window: 0.016124646 m / 1.25 s = 12.90 mm/s. Using the NET displacement instead gives 0.014577281 m / 1.25 s = 11.66 mm/s and Re = 581 rather than 643. Both are stated so a recomputation does not look like a discrepancy; path length is the right choice here because Re is about the speed at which the body moves through the fluid, not about how far it ends up from where it started.

reciprocity.method: T(t) = sin(wt) u + cos(wt) v with u=cos(phi), v=sin(phi); the control traces a closed curve in span{u,v}; rank <= 1 means a retraced segment, i.e. time-reciprocal
reciprocity.why: five of the six patterns assign only the phases 0 and pi, so every voxel's temperature is +/- A sin(wt): the whole body is driven by ONE scalar in time and the shape sequence is a path retraced in reverse. Only 'travelling' uses phi = 2 pi x / nx, which gives five distinct phases.

quasistatic_margin.why_it_matters: the reciprocity result above is about the CONTROL T_i(t). It transfers to the SHAPE only if the body's elastic response has no spatially varying phase lag. A flexible body whose elastic relaxation time is comparable to the drive period CAN swim on a reciprocal control (the elastohydrodynamic escape from the scallop theorem), so this gate is load-bearing.

real_tissue_estimate.status: E_Pa is ASSUMED (order-of-magnitude soft tissue); not measured here

fluid_driven_deformation_number.definition: mu * omega / E, the ratio of viscous stress from the surrounding water to the body's elastic stress
fluid_driven_deformation_number.reading: both are many orders below 1, so the surrounding water cannot appreciably deform the body and the shape follows the imposed rest sizes quasi-statically

stokes_ranking.model: RPY bead swimmer, 45 beads of radius s/2 at the voxel centres, shapes from a quasi-static free-floating elastic relaxation of the same actuation law

dry_friction_ranking.source: artifacts/voxel-actuation/summary.json arm_A, read not recomputed; and reproduced bit-for-bit here for travelling (0.0145773 m)

M2_longitudinal_plus_phase_gradient.must: become non-zero (it is now non-reciprocal); proves the zeros are not a solver that always returns zero

M3_free_draining_no_hydrodynamic_interac.must: give 0 for every gait: a free-draining body cannot swim

M4_time_reversed_travelling.must: flip sign exactly (kinematic reversibility of Stokes flow)

stokes_analytic_controls.SP2_note: Najafi-Golestanian three-sphere swimmer. We check the SCALING exponents (proportional to a, to d1, to d2, and to L^-2) rather than a prefactor, because we did not retrieve the published prefactor's full text. Deviations of a few percent are the expected finite-amplitude correction at d/L = 0.1.

stokes_invariance_checks.expectation: Stokes flow is linear and has no intrinsic scale, so displacement per cycle in BODY LENGTHS must be independent of absolute size, of viscosity and of frequency. Sensitivity to k2_ratio is the lattice's elastic-constant dependence and is reported, not suppressed.

stokes_shape_tolerance_refinement.why: the five reciprocal gaits must give EXACTLY zero. What the solver returns for them is the numerical residue of an iterative elastic relaxation, not a displacement. This arm separates the two: tighten the shape solve and a residue falls while a real displacement does not.
stokes_shape_tolerance_refinement.reading: travelling is stable to four significant figures across four decades of tolerance; the three reciprocal gaits fall by three to four orders of magnitude, tracking the tolerance, and floor near 1e-8 where double precision runs out. The reciprocal gaits' values are therefore reported as ZERO TO THE PRECISION OF THE SHAPE SOLVE and MUST NOT be ranked against each other.

ranking_comparison.spearman_caveat: computed over all six, but FIVE of the six Stokes values are numerical zero, so their relative order is meaningless and this coefficient is reported only to show that a naive correlation looks reassuring while the underlying comparison is vacuous. It is not evidence of transfer.
ranking_comparison.verdict: the dry-friction ranking does NOT transfer. Its 2nd and 3rd places (longitudinal 0.1532 BL, lateral 0.1412 BL) are both time-reciprocal and give exactly zero in the Stokes limit. Only the 1st place, travelling, survives the regime change.

data.headline: A millimetre-scale living construct sits at Reynolds number below 0.1, and five of the six published actuation patterns are time-reciprocal, so Purcell's scallop theorem makes their net displacement exactly zero there. The published gait ranking does not transfer: its 2nd and 3rd places are both dead in the regime the real object occupies, and only the travelling wave survives.

the_simulated_object_is_also_the_wrong_S.why_this_is_worth_stating_beside_the_Rey: Re = 643 is an abstraction. The plain fact underneath it is checkable from the committed candidate file and may land harder: the simulated body is 40-50 mm and a real construct is 0.5-1 mm, so the artifact simulates an object roughly 40 to 100 times too large, quite apart from having no fluid in it.
the_simulated_object_is_also_the_wrong_S.real_source: Gumuskaya et al. 2023 (PMID 38032125) report anthrobot diameters of 30-500 um; 1 mm is the nominal xenobot figure and is ASSUMED, not read from a paper

the_spearman_trap.what: A rank correlation between the two regimes' gait orderings returns rho = 0.943 with p = 0.005, which reads as excellent transfer.
the_spearman_trap.why_it_is_vacuous: five of the six Stokes values are the same number - exactly zero - so their relative order carries no information at all. The coefficient is computed over a tie that the test treats as a ranking.
the_spearman_trap.why_it_is_worth_its_own_section: this is a statistic reporting excellent agreement at the exact moment agreement has failed completely, and failed QUALITATIVELY rather than by degree. Anyone checking 'did the ranking transfer?' with a rank correlation would conclude that it did.
the_spearman_trap.what_to_do_instead: ask how many of the ranked items are distinguishable at all before ranking them. Here the answer is one, and the comparison should never have been posed as a correlation.

model.what_it_is: two models and one exact classification. (1) A closed-form Reynolds-number evaluation. (2) An exact algebraic test of whether each published actuation pattern is time-reciprocal. (3) A Rotne-Prager-Yamakawa bead-model Stokes swimmer over shapes from a quasi-static, free-floating, central-force spring lattice driven by the same actuation law.
model.not_voxelyze: the Stokes swimmer is OUR code and is not Voxelyze. Voxelyze at its pin is used unmodified for the dry-friction comparison, and reproduces the published travelling-wave run bit-for-bit at 0.0145773 m against 0.014577281 m.

limitations: The scallop-theorem result applies to a FREE SWIMMER. A construct crawling on a dish with its ventral surface in contact is not one: contact friction is not Stokes drag and is outside the theorem's assumptions, so a reciprocal gait can rectify against a surface. Kriegman et al. 2020 state their deciliated organisms 'always kept part of their ventral surfaces in contact with the surface of the dish due to negative buoyancy'.

Most published constructs are cilia-driven, and cilia are a SURFACE thrust mechanism, not a body gait. Kriegman et al. 2021's own simulation models them as an impulse force on each surface voxel. Our analysis bears directly on the 2020 cardiac-driven constructs, which do deform, and only indirectly on the cilia-driven ones.

The reciprocity test is exact for the CONTROL sequence. Carrying it to the SHAPE needs quasi-static response, which we check numerically rather than assume. The gate is met but only by a factor of 2.5 to 7 on the elastic-relaxation ratio, not by orders of magnitude; the fluid-driven deformation number mu*omega/E is the one that clears by many orders.

The elastic lattice is central-force, so it obeys the Cauchy relations and its Poisson ratio is a property of the spring topology rather than an input. We measure 0.20 against the artifact's 0.35, and its axial and bending effective moduli differ by about 2x. It is used only to generate a shape.
The reciprocal gaits return 1e-7 to 1e-8 rather than literal zero, which is the numerical residue of an iterative shape solve, not a displacement. Their relative order carries no information.
Water at 20 C is assumed for every fluid property. Real media differ, and a non-Newtonian medium would partially lift the scallop-theorem constraint (Qiu et al. 2014, PMID 25369018).
The Reynolds number for the simulated artifact body is a SCALE COMPARISON. That simulation contains no fluid at all.
what_this_cannot_establish: that any real construct would or would not move; no organism was measured
a corrected gait ranking for a surface crawler, which is a different problem
anything about cilia-driven propulsion, whose stroke we did not model
that the travelling wave is buildable: no living construct has per-region actuation phase control

not_diverged_gate.what: every Voxelyze run behind these studies is checked for divergence. Voxelyze's doTimeStep returns false when any link's axial strain exceeds 100; the driver records that as diverged and exits 3. A diverged run is not evidence and none is used.
not_diverged_gate.note: regime-check's own Stokes and elastic solves are not time-stepped and cannot diverge; their analogue is the minimiser-convergence flag in elastic_lattice_controls and the shape-solve tolerance refinement arm.

Everywhere a published construct actually sits, Re is at most about 0.1: inertia is irrelevant and viscosity dominates. The simulated body that the published gait ranking came from would be at Re = 643 in water, 3.8 orders of magnitude away. That simulation contains no fluid at all, so this is a comparison of scales rather than a property of it.

figures.alt: Two dot plots side by side on a shared logarithmic axis, one for dry friction and one for Stokes flow, listing six gaits. Under dry friction all six have non-zero values from 0.073 down to 4e-6 body lengths per cycle. Under Stokes flow only the travelling wave has a value, 0.034; the other five are marked with open circles and arrows pointing off-scale labelled exactly zero.

In Stokes flow the longitudinal split does not work at all, because it is time-reciprocal. Note the trap: Spearman's rho over all six is 0.94 with p = 0.005, which reads as excellent transfer and is vacuous, because five of the six Stokes values are the same number.

studies.title: It does not converge, and the flagged swing was the encoding
studies.question: An independent audit recorded a 7.25-fold change in net displacement under grid refinement and left spatial convergence unresolved, and flagged a body-size series that swung ten-fold without trending. Does the model converge on a clean refinement series, and is that swing a gait-length resonance or a numerical artifact?
studies.summary: It does not converge, and the swing is neither of the offered options: it is the actuation encoding. On a parity-matched refinement, holding the outer envelope and the physical actuation field fixed while refining the lattice four-fold from 45 to 2880 voxels, the travelling wave spans 41% of its coarsest value and the longitudinal split 54%, and both series turn over rather than settling. The winner is stable across all four levels but the margin falls from 19.4 to 10.4 times and is still moving at the finest grid. The flagged swing resolves cleanly: the longitudinal pattern splits the body at index nx/2, so odd nx gives an asymmetric actuator layout and even nx a symmetric one, and sweeping nx from 3 to 16 reveals two smooth monotone branches interleaved. Two discriminators declared in advance both fail for a resonance: the alternation is absent from the travelling wave, whose phase does not depend on parity, by a median factor of 1.008 against 20.3; and the optimum frequency does not move with body length, sitting at 12 Hz for both nx = 4 and nx = 8 while the body doubles. The weakness is that only two of six patterns were refined, so this cannot offer a corrected ranking, and four levels can show a series failing to settle but cannot extract a trustworthy convergence order.

predeclared_questions: Q1 does a parity-matched refinement series converge, and at what observed order
Q2 resonance or encoding; discriminators D1 (must appear in travelling) and D2 (optimum must scale as 1/L)
Q3 is the gait ranking stable under refinement

refinement_series.design: the outer envelope and the PHYSICAL actuation field are held fixed while the lattice is refined. Series A uses travelling, whose phase 2*pi*x/nx is a function of fractional position and so is identical on every grid. Series B uses longitudinal with EVEN nx only, so the split at index nx/2 falls at the same physical plane (x = 20 mm) on every grid: 2x10 = 4x5 = 6x3.333 = 8x2.5 mm. The published artifact refined nx 5 -> 10, which moved that plane from 20 to 25 mm and flipped its parity at the same time.
refinement_series.denominator_note: normalised by the OUTER ENVELOPE nx*voxel, which is invariant across the series. The artifact's stored metric divides by the centre-to-centre span (nx-1)*voxel, which is NOT invariant, and its own audit records that comparing two runs under two different denominators manufactured an agreement that was not in the data.

parity_sweep.fixed: voxel 10 mm, freq 4 Hz, 5 cycles, same material

D1_alternation_must_appear_in_travelling.verdict: FAILS for a resonance: longitudinal alternates by a median factor of 20.3, travelling by 1.008, i.e. not at all.

each_parity_branch_is_monotone.reading: the series the audit called non-monotone is TWO smooth monotone branches interleaved; the four points it flagged (nx 4,5,6,7) are two adjacent points of each branch

D2_optimum_frequency_must_scale_as_1_ove.verdict: FAILS for a resonance: body length rises by 2.33x from nx=4 to nx=8 and longitudinal's optimum frequency is 12.0 Hz at both ends. A length resonance requires f_opt to fall by the same factor.
D2_optimum_frequency_must_scale_as_1_ove.travelling_caveat: travelling's optimum runs to the lowest swept frequency for nx>=5, so it is a BOUNDARY not an optimum; its total variation over 0.25-16 Hz is at most 0.63, a broad shallow response rather than a peak.

mechanism_named_at_the_source.file: scripts/voxel_actuation/soft_actuation.cpp, phaseFor(), the 'longitudinal' branch (and the identical 'lateral' and 'dorsoventral' branches with y and z)
mechanism_named_at_the_source.the_operator: c.nx/2 is C++ INTEGER division. For even nx it splits the body exactly in half; for odd nx it cannot, and leaves one extra plane of voxels on one side.
mechanism_named_at_the_source.why_it_produces_two_branches: an unbalanced split leaves a net actuation dipole along the travel axis; a balanced one cancels it to leading order. Net translation needs that broken mirror symmetry, so the odd-nx bodies move roughly an order of magnitude further than their even-nx neighbours at identical resolution, material, amplitude and duration.
mechanism_named_at_the_source.why_travelling_is_immune: its phase is 2*pi*x/nx, a continuous function of fractional position along the body. It never divides by 2 and has no parity to be odd or even, which is why the alternation is absent from it by a median factor of 1.008.
mechanism_named_at_the_source.why_no_frequency_removes_it: the asymmetry is in the spatial actuator LAYOUT, not in the timing, so changing the drive frequency cannot cancel it - and does not, from 0.25 to 16 Hz.
mechanism_named_at_the_source.credit: the integer-division operator was identified by the team lead reading the driver source; this study had established the two-branch structure and its three discriminators without naming the line.

parity_vs_resonance.verdict: ENCODING, not resonance and not a solver artifact. The alternation appears only in the pattern whose phase assignment depends on grid parity; it is absent from the pattern whose phase is a continuous function of position; each parity branch is smooth and monotone over 14 values; and it persists unchanged at every drive frequency from 0.25 to 16 Hz. It is a real mechanical consequence of a real difference in actuator layout, and that difference is an artifact of writing the split as an index comparison.

data.headline: On a parity-matched refinement series the model does NOT converge. Across a 4x refinement (45 to 2880 voxels) the travelling wave spans 41% of its coarsest value and the longitudinal split 54%, and BOTH series turn over rather than settling. Separately, the non-monotone body-size series the independent audit flagged is the actuation encoding, not a gait-length resonance: it is two smooth monotone branches interleaved by the parity of the actuator split, it is absent from the pattern whose phase does not depend on parity, and it does not move with drive frequency.

Q1_verdict.statement: neither series converges. Both are non-monotone across four levels and the successive differences do not fall the way a converging series' do: series A gives ratios 1.44 then 0.83, series B 0.91 then 0.59. A power-law fit f(h) = f0 + C h^p returns p = 0.05 for series A with a residual of 3.4e-2 against values near 0.3, which is not a convergence order but a statement that the series is not a power law.
Q1_verdict.what_the_audit_said: the independent audit recorded G_actual_SI_coarse_to_fine_ratio = 7.25 and the status line 'spatial G unresolved'. This study resolves it, as a NEGATIVE: most of that 7.25 was the parity confound, and what remains still does not converge.
Q1_verdict.consequence_for_the_published_artifact: any net displacement quoted from the coarse 5x3x3 grid is provisional at best. The artifact itself predicted no convergence for its arm G and said so in advance, so this is a confirmation of its own stated expectation rather than a contradiction of a claim it made.

ranking_stability.reading: the ORDER is stable - travelling is ahead of longitudinal at every one of the four levels - but the SIZE of the gap is not: it falls from 19.4x to 10.4x across the refinement and is STILL MOVING at the finest grid, with the last step (11.7 to 10.4) no smaller than the one before it relative to the remaining gap. The margin has therefore NOT converged either.
ranking_stability.what_is_and_is_not_quotable: 'travelling beats longitudinal' is supported at every level tested. 'travelling beats longitudinal by N times' is NOT quotable at any N, because the margin has not converged and the sequence gives no reason to believe 10.4 is closer to the limit than 19.4 was.
ranking_stability.what_can_be_said: this study refines TWO patterns, not all six, so it cannot report a full ranking at the fine grid. What it establishes is the prior question: whether a single pattern's value is stable enough for any ranking drawn from the coarse grid to mean anything.

timestep_separation_arm.why: a refinement at fixed dtScale halves dt automatically with the lattice, so spatial and temporal error are confounded. This arm repeats levels 1-3 of both series at HALF the timestep and asks whether the spatial spread survives.
timestep_separation_arm.verdict: For the travelling wave the non-convergence is unambiguously SPATIAL: halving dt changes any level by at most 1.3% while the spread across levels 1-3 is 22% (41% over all four), and that spread is essentially unchanged at the finer dt, 22.4% against 21.8%. For the longitudinal split the temporal error is NOT negligible - up to 15.5% at level 2 - but it does not explain the spread either: halving dt moves it only from 54.4% to 48.5%. Spatial error dominates by about 17x for travelling and about 3.5x for longitudinal.
timestep_separation_arm.relation_to_the_artifacts_own_arm_F: the pinned artifact's timestep arm found 0.90% spread across a 4x dt range, which does not conflict with the 5.3% we see at B1. Arm F ran longitudinal at nx=5, the ASYMMETRIC split, whose net displacement is large (0.153 body lengths). B1 is nx=4, the SYMMETRIC split, an order of magnitude smaller at 0.015 normalised, so the same absolute numerical error is a much larger relative one. The two measure the same thing on configurations separated by the parity effect this study is about.
timestep_separation_arm.caveat: level 4 was not repeated at the finer timestep.

conditioning_arm.status: POST-HOC. Found by cross-checking the local refinement against an independent run of the same series on a Nebius L40S node, where two of fourteen runs disagreed.
conditioning_arm.what_happened: 12 of the 14 runs were bit-identical between an AWS host and a Nebius node, confirming the engine is deterministic across machines as the protocol claims. The two that disagreed were exactly the level-3 grids, where voxel = 1/300 m: the local runs passed the full double-precision value and the remote job passed a 10-digit literal. Re-running locally with the 10-digit value reproduces the remote result EXACTLY, so the engine is not at fault and the difference is entirely the input spelling.
conditioning_arm.reading: A relative perturbation of 1.0e-8 in the voxel size changes net displacement by 1.2e-2 for the SYMMETRIC longitudinal split - an amplification of about 1.2e6 - and by 1.1e-4 for the travelling wave, an amplification of about 1.1e4. The quantity being refined is therefore not a well-conditioned function of the inputs at these configurations, and the symmetric split is roughly 100x worse than the travelling wave. That is a direct explanation for why the refinement series do not converge, and it predicts that no amount of further refinement would make them: the spread is not dominated by discretisation error that shrinks with h.
conditioning_arm.caveat: this is ONE perturbation of ONE parameter at ONE grid level per pattern. It establishes that the configuration is ill-conditioned; it does not measure a condition number, and the amplification figures should not be quoted as one.
conditioning_arm.consequence_for_the_series: the series reported here all use the full double-precision 1/300 locally, so they are internally consistent. A reader reproducing them must pass the same value; a 10-digit literal changes level 3 by 1.2% for longitudinal.

what_this_cannot_establish: that the model converges. It refines two of six patterns on three or four levels each; a converged value is not demonstrated and is not claimed.
a corrected ranking of the six gaits. Only travelling and longitudinal were refined.

anything about a biological construct. This is the same generic soft-voxel model throughout, with the same assumed parameters, and the regime-check study shows it is not the regime a real construct occupies.

that the parity effect is the ONLY cause of the artifact's 8.2x arm-G gap. Varying nx at fixed voxel size changes count, length and mass together, as the independent audit already noted; this study adds that the effect is absent from a parity-free pattern and frequency-independent, which rules out a resonance but does not isolate a single cause.

limitations: Two patterns were refined, not six. No corrected ranking of the six gaits is offered or possible from this.

Four levels is enough to show that a series does not settle; it is not enough to extract a reliable convergence order, and the power-law fits here have residuals of 5% and more, which is itself the finding.

Temporal and spatial error ARE separated, by a half-timestep repeat of levels 1-3 (see timestep_separation_arm): spatial dominates by about 17x for the travelling wave and 3.5x for the longitudinal split, and the spatial spread survives at the finer timestep. Two caveats: level 4 was not repeated at the finer timestep, and for longitudinal the temporal error is NOT negligible, reaching 15.5% at level 2.

Varying nx at fixed voxel size, which is how the parity sweep is done, changes voxel count, body length and mass together. The independent audit already noted this. We add that the effect is absent from a parity-free pattern and is frequency-independent, which rules out a gait-length resonance; it does not isolate a single cause.

The frequency optima for the travelling wave sit at the lowest swept frequency for nx >= 5, so they are boundaries rather than optima and are labelled as such. The longitudinal optima are interior, which is what the D2 discriminator rests on.
This is the generic soft-voxel model with assumed parameters throughout. Our own regime-check study finds it is not the regime a real construct occupies.

figures.alt: Three panels. The first shows the travelling wave's normalised displacement across four refinement levels at 45, 360, 1215 and 2880 voxels, rising then falling, spread 41 per cent. The second shows the parity-matched longitudinal split across 36, 288, 972 and 2304 voxels, rising then falling, spread 54 per cent. The third shows the ratio between them falling from 19.4 to 10.4 across the same levels.
figures.caption: Simulation. A parity-matched grid refinement, four levels, outer envelope and physical actuation field held fixed. Neither series settles: both turn over, and the successive differences do not fall the way a converging series' do. The published artifact instead refined nx from 5 to 10, which moved its actuation split from 20 mm to 25 mm and flipped its parity at the same time. Removing that confound does not produce convergence; it only shows that convergence was never the thing being measured.

figures.alt: Three panels. The top sweeps nx from 3 to 16 on a log axis: longitudinal alternates sharply between an upper odd-nx branch and a lower even-nx branch, each smooth and monotone, while the travelling wave is a single smooth curve with no alternation. The lower left shows travelling's frequency response from 0.25 to 16 Hz at four body lengths, broad and shallow. The lower right plots the optimum frequency against body length, showing longitudinal flat at 12 Hz against a dashed 1/L reference.
figures.caption: Simulation. The flagged non-monotonicity is the actuation encoding, not the mechanics and not the solver. The four points the audit flagged are two adjacent points of each smooth branch. Both predeclared discriminators fail for a resonance: the alternation does not appear in the parity-free pattern, and the optimum frequency does not scale with body length.

studies.title: Does the best self-mover also push best?
studies.question: Every headline xenobot result is about the construct moving itself. What body plan and actuation pattern lets it do useful mechanical work on an external object, and is the published optimisation target the right one for the application?
studies.summary: Our predeclared expectation was that the best self-mover would not be the best pusher. It was wrong, and we report it as a failed prediction. The travelling wave is first on every metric: 103.6 mm of cargo moved against 35.8 and 21.7 mm, a transport ratio of 0.95 of its own path transferred to the cargo against 0.51 and 0.26, and seven times the useful work per unit of actuation energy. What the study did find is that the live constraint is reach rather than push — with the cargo one clear lattice site away, only one gait of six covers that distance in the artifact's own five cycles, so a contact-gated forty-cycle arm was added to separate the two — and that all three contacting gaits stall at the same 64 g cargo with efficiency peaking just below it, so the heaviest load that still moves is the right one to carry. The swarm arm returns an honest negative: a uniform swarm sweeps but does not corral, with the particle field's radius of gyration increasing in 28 of 30 runs, and the one apparent exception — 2 of 5 seeds at the largest swarm size — tested rather than hedged and shown to be a field-size effect rather than an onset. The weakness is that all of it is in the dry-friction regime, which our own first study says is not the regime a real construct occupies; in water, four of the six gaits compared here could not push anything at all.
studies.code: results/xenobot/code/cargo_actuation.cpp, code/cargo_work.py, code/cargo_contact.py, code/cargo_mass.py, code/cargo_swarm.py, code/cargo_assemble.py

data.headline: In this dry-friction model the body plan that moves itself best also pushes best: the travelling wave wins on cargo displacement, on transport ratio and on energy efficiency, contradicting our predeclared expectation. The real design gate is not which gait ranks highest but whether the gait moves an external object at all, and in 5 cycles only one of six even reaches its cargo. A uniform swarm never corrals, over swarm sizes 1 to 16 in two field sizes.

declared_metrics.M5: transport ratio = cargo net displacement / construct path length
declared_metrics.S1_primary_swarm: mean particle net displacement vs swarm size N
declared_metrics.S2: change in particle radius of gyration (negative = aggregation)

predeclared_expectation.statement: the gait that moves the construct itself furthest will NOT be the gait that pushes an external object furthest
predeclared_expectation.evidence: travelling is first on every metric in arm 1b: cargo displacement 103.6 mm vs 35.8 mm (longitudinal) and 21.7 mm (lateral); transport ratio 0.947 vs 0.508 and 0.260; efficiency 0.0326 vs 0.0114 and 0.0044. The ordering is identical to the self-locomotion ordering and the gap is WIDER in pushing than in self-locomotion.
predeclared_expectation.note: We record this as a failed prediction rather than reframing it. One pilot run of the travelling pattern was executed as a plumbing check before the metrics were written down, and its cargo displacement was seen; every other number here was produced afterwards.

C2_cargo_out_of_reach_must_not_move.gate: cargo <= 1e-9 m while the construct still moves

C5b_swarm_zero_amplitude_fixed_geometry.gate: particles must not move with the actuation off

C6_degenerate_swarm_geometry_refused.what: the driver exits 4 if any construct is placed outside the particle field, because swarm size would then not be the only variable
C6_degenerate_swarm_geometry_refused.why_it_exists: the FIRST version of the swarm arm auto-spread constructs over a square field and silently pushed the outermost ones outside it at N=6 and N=8, which returned bit-identical particle outcomes for those two sizes. That run is discarded and not reported.
C6_degenerate_swarm_geometry_refused.verified: running 8 constructs against a field of half-width 5 sites prints the FATAL line and refuses

arm1_reach_limited_5_cycles.finding: at the artifact's own 5 cycles the arm measures REACH, not push. The cargo's nearest surface sits 7.5 mm from the construct's (one clear lattice site, minus two 6.25 mm collision envelopes) and only the travelling wave covers that distance in 5 cycles. Every other gait scores exactly zero because it never arrives.
arm1_reach_limited_5_cycles.engineering_reading: this is a real result and not only an artifact of our geometry: a construct that moves slowly never reaches its workpiece within its working life. It is reported separately from the push question rather than mixed into it.

arm1b_contact_gated_40_cycles.design: contact window starts at the first measurement sample where the cargo COM has moved more than 1 um; transport ratio and efficiency are computed over that window only

reach_and_push_are_different_quantities.why_they_are_reported_separately: time-to-contact and work-after-contact are different engineering quantities, and a body plan can be good at one and bad at the other. Collapsing them into a single cargo-displacement number hides which one a design is losing on, and in the 5-cycle arm it hid the fact that five of six gaits were losing on REACH and had not been tested on push at all.
reach_and_push_are_different_quantities.reach_gate: does the construct arrive at the workpiece within its working life? Measured here as time to first cargo motion above 1 um, with the cargo 7.5 mm of clear space away.
reach_and_push_are_different_quantities.push_gate: given contact, how much of the construct's own motion and energy reaches the cargo? Measured over the post-contact window only.
reach_and_push_are_different_quantities.commercial_reading: The two orderings are NOT the same, which is the reason for reporting them apart. Travelling is first on both. But between the two reciprocal gaits the order swaps: lateral reaches the cargo FIRST (1.71 s against longitudinal's 1.79 s) and then pushes WORST, transferring 0.26 of its own path against longitudinal's 0.51. So arriving sooner and pushing better are separable properties here, and a cargo-displacement number alone would have hidden it.

size_of_the_swap.honest_scale: the reach difference between those two is about 4.8%, which is small and rests on a single contact-threshold crossing per gait with no seed spread (this model has no RNG). The push difference is about 2x and is the robust half of the comparison. Do not read the reach swap as a strong result.

arm2b_cargo_mass.design: cargo density scaled 0.25x to 32x at fixed volume (8 voxels), placed one clear lattice site away in each gait's OWN direction of travel, 40 cycles so contact is guaranteed

metric_correction.problem: our declared efficiency M4 uses the cargo's PATH LENGTH, so a stalled cargo that is merely jiggled back and forth still accumulates friction work. Past the stall threshold M4 therefore RISES while transport collapses: travelling at 256 g reports the highest M4 of the whole sweep (0.134) while moving the cargo 0.105 mm.
metric_correction.fix: we add efficiency_directed, which uses the cargo's NET displacement instead, a stricter lower bound on useful directed work. Both are reported; M4 is the declared metric and is not deleted.
metric_correction.rule: M4 is meaningful only BELOW the stall threshold.

arm2b_cargo_mass.ranking_change_is_not_real: the ordering of longitudinal and lateral swaps only at 128 g and 256 g, where BOTH are stalled and both move the cargo by less than 0.25 mm. That is a swap between two noise-floor values, not a reversal, and it must not be reported as the ranking depending on cargo mass.

arm3_swarm.design: N constructs evenly spread along y inside a FIXED rectangular particle field (x -16..+2, y -22..+22 lattice sites) holding 120 single-voxel passive particles; 40 actuation cycles; 5 seeds; every construct runs the travelling gait. The field is offset to -x because that is the direction all these gaits travel, so the swept and seeded regions coincide.
arm3_swarm.S1_scaling_reading: mean particle displacement scales as N^1.15 over N = 1 to 8, i.e. very slightly superlinear. Eight constructs move 9.3x as much material as one.

S4_energy_efficiency_flat.reading: friction work done on the field per unit actuation work is 0.0066-0.0102 across the whole range and does not improve with swarm size. A bigger swarm moves more material because it spends more energy, not because it spends it better.

S2_aggregation.effect_size_caution: State this as an effect size, not as a mechanism. The median change is 0.22% to 0.77% of the field's radius of gyration, and it is NOT monotone in N: N=8 sits below N=6 and barely above N=1. A sub-1% change that does not scale with swarm size is 'the field barely moves', not dispersal. For scale, the particles' centre of mass travels 1.9 to 19 mm over the run while a construct travels 116 mm. The defensible claim is NO AGGREGATION AT ANY N; the word 'disperses' invites a reader to think a mechanism was identified, and none was.
S2_aggregation.verdict: NO aggregation. The particle field's radius of gyration INCREASED in 28 of the 30 runs. Both exceptions are at the largest swarm size, N=8, where 2 of 5 seeds turn negative (-0.111 and -0.457 mm) and the median dispersion falls 2.6-fold from its N=6 value. That is a possible ONSET rather than scatter, and it is tested in the follow-up arm rather than left as a hedge.
S2_aggregation.mechanism: every construct runs the same gait and travels the same way, so their contributions add as a common drift rather than converging. Corralling needs either a concave body that traps material, as the published semitoroidal progenitor has, or constructs that move differently from one another.
S2_aggregation.scope: this is a statement about a uniform, sensorless, single-gait swarm in this model. It is not a statement about swarms.
S2_aggregation.onset_tested: The two aggregating seeds at N=8 in the main arm are a BOUNDARY effect, not an onset: the same swarm size in a wider field shows nothing, and a larger swarm in the wider field also shows nothing. Aggregation-like behaviour appears only when the swarm spans more than about 0.8 of the field.

limitations: This is the dry-friction regime - Coulomb friction on a rigid floor under gravity, plus a numerical absolute-frame damping term - matching the artifact it extends. Our own regime-check study finds that a real millimetre-scale construct sits at Reynolds number below 0.1, where four of the six gaits compared here produce exactly zero displacement and could not push anything at all. Every number in this study is inside a model the first study says is the wrong regime.

The cargo gap is one lattice site because that is the minimum that avoids Voxelyze linking the two bodies into one. That sets a 7.5 mm clear distance the construct must cross before any pushing happens, which is why arm 1 is reach-limited and arm 1b exists.

W_actuation is the axial term only: bending and torsion rest states are not actuated so they do no actuation work, but they do store and dissipate energy that is not counted. The actuation efficiency is therefore an UPPER bound on the fraction of total input energy delivered.
W_cargo_friction is a closed form that ignores collision damping and any kinetic energy left in the cargo at the end, so it is a LOWER bound on work done on the cargo.

Our declared efficiency metric M4 breaks down past the stall threshold, for the reason recorded above. We found this by running the sweep far enough to stall rather than stopping at a mass where the metric still behaved.
The swarm's particles are single voxels on the floor with the same friction and density as the construct. Nothing is calibrated to cells, debris or microplastic.

Voxelyze has no random number generator and this driver's only randomness is our own seeded particle placement, so the seed spread reported here is spread over ARENAS, not over mechanics. Repeat runs at a fixed seed are bitwise identical.

The swarm result covers N = 1 to 16 in two field sizes. Its one apparent exception, 2 of 5 seeds at N = 8 in the narrower field, was tested rather than hedged and turned out to track the swarm's span relative to the arena rather than its size. The threshold is bracketed between span/field 0.68 and 0.84, not located, and two field widths is not a scan over field width.
what_this_cannot_establish: that any construct would push anything in water, which is the regime that matters
that a real xenobot or anthrobot can transport a defined cargo; no published one has
a force, a modulus or a transport rate for any organism
that a swarm cannot aggregate - only that this uniform single-gait swarm does not

arm3b_onset_test.status: POST-HOC. Declared after seeing the N=8 result in the main arm, and reported as a diagnosis rather than as confirmatory evidence.
arm3b_onset_test.why: In the main arm the field dispersed at every N from 1 to 6 in all seeds, then at N=8 the median fell 2.6-fold and 2 of 5 seeds turned negative. That is either the onset of aggregation at larger swarm size or something else. N>9 does not fit the main arm's field at the minimum construct stride, so this arm widens the field in y, scales the particle count to hold DENSITY fixed, and pushes N to 16.
arm3b_onset_test.predeclared_for_this_arm: an onset predicts the median rg change keeps falling with N and crosses zero; seed scatter predicts the median stays positive with a wide spread
arm3b_onset_test.automatic_verdict_from_the_arm_script: NOT a monotone onset; consistent with seed scatter
arm3b_onset_test.automatic_verdict_superseded: the script's own test was whether the median falls monotonically with N and crosses zero. It does not (0.379, 0.466, 0.442, 0.051 mm at N = 4, 8, 12, 16), so the script returned 'consistent with seed scatter'. Pooling both fields gives a better explanation, below, and that is what is reported.

span_analysis.hypothesis: the apparent aggregation is a BOUNDARY effect: it appears when the swarm spans most of the field, so the constructs sweep particles into a narrower band, regardless of N.
span_analysis.measure: swarm half-span in lattice sites divided by field half-width; constructs sit at stride 5 in y
span_analysis.the_controlled_comparison: N = 8 is the discriminator. In the narrow field its span/field is 0.84 and 2 of 5 seeds aggregate; in the wide field the SAME swarm size has span/field 0.44 and 0 of 5 aggregate. Conversely N = 12 in the wide field is a LARGER swarm at span/field 0.68 and also shows nothing. So the effect tracks the span ratio and not the swarm size.
span_analysis.verdict: NOT a swarm-size onset. Across 10 configurations in two field sizes and swarm sizes 1 to 16, every configuration with span/field <= 0.68 gives 0 aggregating seeds, and both configurations with span/field >= 0.84 give some (2/5 and 1/5) with the median collapsing. The main arm's conclusion therefore stands and is strengthened: a uniform, sensorless, single-gait swarm does not corral. What looked like aggregation is the swarm reaching the edge of its arena.
span_analysis.caveat: the cut sits between 0.68 and 0.84 with no configuration in between, so the threshold is bracketed rather than located, and 'span/field' is one summary of a geometry that also changes particle count per construct. Two field widths is not a scan over field width.

arm3b_onset_test.reading: The two aggregating seeds at N=8 in the main arm are a BOUNDARY effect, not an onset: the same swarm size in a wider field shows nothing, and a larger swarm in the wider field also shows nothing. Aggregation-like behaviour appears only when the swarm spans more than about 0.8 of the field.

not_diverged_gate.what: every Voxelyze run behind these studies is checked for divergence. Voxelyze's doTimeStep returns false when any link's axial strain exceeds 100; the driver records that as diverged and exits 3. A diverged run is not evidence and none is used.

studies.summary_table_title: Self-locomotion against cargo transport, per gait

figures.alt: Two panels. The upper shows paired horizontal bars per gait for self-locomotion and cargo displacement over 40 cycles: travelling 117.4 and 103.6 mm, longitudinal 47.5 and 35.8, lateral 43.4 and 21.7, and three gaits marked as never having reached the cargo. The lower shows two separate bar charts for the three contacting gaits, transport ratio from 0.95 down to 0.26 and efficiency from 3.26 down to 0.44 per cent.
figures.caption: Simulation, dry friction. The best self-mover is also the best pusher, contradicting our predeclared expectation, and its advantage is larger in pushing than in self-locomotion. Three of six gaits never reach the cargo at all even in forty cycles, which is a reach result rather than a push result and is reported separately for that reason.

figures.alt: Two panels against swarm size from one to eight constructs, each with a min-to-max band over five seeds. The left shows mean particle displacement rising from about 2 to 19 mm, slightly faster than linear. The right shows the change in the particle field's radius of gyration staying positive at every swarm size, with a shaded region below zero labelled as where aggregation would appear and a single seed at N equals eight dipping into it.
figures.caption: Simulation, dry friction. A uniform swarm sweeps; it does not corral. Material moved rises slightly faster than linearly with swarm size, but energy efficiency is flat and the particle field disperses in 28 of 30 runs. The two exceptions, both at the largest swarm size here, prompted a follow-up arm in a density-matched wider field out to 16 constructs; it found no aggregation at any swarm size, so the exceptions were a property of the narrower field rather than of swarm size. Every construct runs the same gait, so their effects add as a common drift rather than converging — which is exactly why the published semitoroidal progenitor, whose concave mouth traps material, aggregates when a uniform swarm does not.

figures.alt: Animation of a top-down simulation: six constructs drawn as clusters of green points travel leftwards through a field of orange points representing passive particles, pushing particles ahead of them and leaving the field more spread out than it started.
figures.caption: Simulation, not a recording. Six constructs on the travelling gait and 120 passive particles under dry Coulomb friction. Voxel centres only — the data hold centres and nothing else, so no orientations, deformed meshes, forces or cellular states are drawn or implied.
